title: commands/ layer imports up into server/tools/_session (resolve_talk_target) — repo-wide dependency inversion
description:
## Problem

The `commands/` layer (L3) imports up into `server/tools/` (L4/presentation),
inverting the dependency arrow (PL-PA-2 / PL-MD-1 / PY-IC-8: core/commands
must never import presentation). This is repo-wide, not isolated:

- `commands/write.py`, `commands/finger.py`, `commands/talk.py` import
  `resolve_talk_target` from `biff.server.tools._session` (defined at
  `server/tools/_session.py:127`) — a pure `@user:tty` addressing function,
  domain logic, not presentation.
- `commands/wall.py` imports `broadcast_wall_to_repos` from
  `biff.server.tools.wall` — a different upward import, same violation class.

## Fix

Move `resolve_talk_target` (and any sibling pure helpers the commands layer
pulls from `server/tools/_session`) DOWN into a core/shared module (e.g.
`src/biff/addressing.py` or a core talk/session module) that both the
commands layer and `server/tools` import, so the arrow points inward
(`server -> core`, `commands -> core`; never `commands -> server`). Assess
`broadcast_wall_to_repos` the same way — either relocate it too or confirm
it's a separate, smaller violation worth its own follow-up. Repoint all
importers; delete the old location(s). Behavior-preserving relocation,
`make check` green.

Surfaced by silent-failure-hunter + code-reviewer on biff-uin (#319);
deliberately NOT fixed there to keep that refactor behavior-preserving and
scoped. Owner: rmh.

title: CLI session identity: adopt a claude-r-style named-session model so ttys and identity persist across invocations
description:
The biff CLI has no stable per-shell session identifier. Every 'biff <cmd>' invocation is a fresh process with no memory of the previous one -- src/biff/cli_session.py:205 unconditionally calls generate_tty() (a fresh random hex) every time. Consequences:

- Two 'biff plan' calls back-to-back from the same shell = two different ttys in /who, both showing as briefly-alive sessions
- tty-based @user:tty addresses rot on every invocation (biff-e04, still open)
- biff-if2 fixed the CLI's user resolution but the every-invocation shell-out to 'gh api user' remains -- swapping GH_TOKEN mid-shell can silently change resolved identity
- Any CLI attempt to satisfy the plan-gate falls back to the leader's SessionHint (biff-ar1 RISK-2) because the CLI has no identity of its own
- The MCP path was solved by biff-7ak (session_id + SessionHint), but the CLI was never threaded onto that mechanism

Discussion arc (leader + operator, 2026-08-09) that this bead captures:

INITIAL DIRECTION -- 'biff login' with shell-PID-keyed state: write ~/.punt-labs/biff/shells/<shell_pid>.json on login, discover via PPID walk on subsequent invocations, dies when the shell dies. Matches SessionHint pattern.

OPERATOR PUSHBACK on the 'block multiple identities per shell' framing: not logical -- every real tool (AWS_PROFILE, GIT_AUTHOR_*, gh auth switch) allows per-invocation identity overrides. Also missed the per-repo dimension entirely -- biff is repo-scoped throughout, a single shell that cd's between repos is already three distinct biff sessions.

OPERATOR PIVOT to a claude-r-style model: separate the session (a first-class named thing with its own lifecycle) from the invocation (any shell can attach to it via -s <id>, any time). This dissolves several problems the shell-binding model couldn't handle cleanly.
notes:
PROPOSED DESIGN SHAPE (claude-r-inspired, needs design mission to formalize):

- biff session new [--tty <name>] [--repo <path>] [--as <user>] creates a session, returns its id (tty name serves as the id since it's already unique-per-user-in-a-repo). State: ~/.punt-labs/biff/sessions/<id>.json = {identity, repo, tty, created_at, expires_at, ...}
- biff -s <id> <cmd> runs against that session's context from any shell, any time -- direct analog of 'claude -r <id>'
- biff (no -s) uses whichever session is 'current' for this shell -- resolved from BIFF_SESSION env var, else ~/.punt-labs/biff/current pointer, else auto-creates a fresh session (preserving today's zero-config UX)
- biff session ls / use <id> / end <id> for lifecycle
- Identity is a property of the session, not the shell -- resolves 'multi-identity per shell' cleanly (create/use a session with a different identity when you need one). Per-invocation override still available via 'biff --as <user> <cmd>' (AWS_PROFILE pattern), unchanged.
- Naming choice: use tty names as session ids, not opaque UUIDs. Users already read/type tty names in /who. Avoids two-namespace confusion between 'session id' and 'tty'.

WHAT THIS FIXES:
- CLI tty stability (main complaint)
- biff-e04 largely closes -- addresses persist as long as the session does, which is now under user control not shell-lifecycle
- biff-if2's residual: identity resolved once at session creation, not per-invocation
- biff-ar1 RISK-2: CLI plan-marker writes can key on a real CLI session identity, not fall back to the leader's SessionHint

DEPENDENCIES / ORDERING:
- The plan-gate fix currently in flight (biff-ar1/biff-om9, missions m-2026-08-09-021 code and m-2026-08-09-023 spec) should land first. Its commands/plan.py change assumes a fallback to SessionHint.resolve_routing_id() -- once this bead lands, commands/plan.py becomes 'prefer CLI session identity if one exists, else fall back to SessionHint,' an additive change.
- Do NOT dispatch this design mission concurrently with the plan-gate work -- same files (commands/plan.py, cli_session.py, session_id.py).

NEEDS STATE-BASED MODELING (per operator, 2026-08-09): this is more state than the code alone captures cleanly. Likely needs a Z-spec extension -- either extending docs/session-model.tex to model the (session_id, tty, identity, repo, created_at) tuple as first-class state with new/use/end transitions, or a new docs/cli-session.tex modeled after claude-code-biff.tex. The design mission for this bead should specify precisely which spec change is needed, so a jms follow-up can formalize it in parallel with implementation (matching the biff-ar1/om9 code-spec parallel-mission pattern this session established).

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP: file a design mission after biff-ar1/om9 lands. Do NOT jump straight to implementation -- the operator's own note is that this needs 'more state-based modeling,' meaning the exact session lifecycle, the transition rules (what does 'use' do if the session is expired/ended? what does 'end' do to messages queued to that session's inbox? does session identity survive across a claude-r-style resume, or is a resume a new session?), and the interaction with the existing tty-resume mechanism (biff-7ak) all need to be nailed down before code.

title: Stable identity+repo addressing: tty-based @user:tty addresses rot on every session restart
description: Reported by claude (quarry session, tty15), 2026-08-09, from a heavy-traffic day (60+ inter-agent messages): tty-based addresses rot whenever a teammate's session restarts, causing sends to bounce or go to a dead session. Hit twice in one day (ethos moved tty5->tty7, biff moved tty19->tty29) and hit the reporter itself while sending the very report ('my first attempt went to claude:tty19, your address from a few hours ago, and bounced'). Needs design work.') and feedback_check_who_before_write.md (mitigation today is 'always /who before /write' — a workaround, not a fix). Aligns with feedback_dont_overscope_routing.md precedent: 'If an id is globally unique, route on it alone; repo/org/tenant are visibility, not routing coordinates' — argues for routing on a stable (identity, repo) pair rather than the volatile tty. title: Shared relay credential defeats DES-046 session-key consent (eavesdrop-then-forge)
description: THREAT MODEL (surfaced by Cursor review on PR #294). The talk consent boundary (DES-046) surfaces a connected/reply frame only when the payload from_key == the ephemeral partner session key. But the default hosted relay uses a SHARED, publicly-bundled credential (src/biff/data/demo.creds) with no per-principal/subject ACLs. So any holder of that credential can (1) wildcard-subscribe (biff.> / biff-dev.talk.notify.>) and eavesdrop cleartext talk frames — learning session keys, from_key/to_key, and bodies — then (2) publish a forged frame claiming an observed partner's from_key. The DES-046 guard COMPARES the claimed key but cannot AUTHENTICATE it, so an eavesdropper who learned the key defeats the guard: cross-org message/prompt injection, forged control frames (end/withdraw), and full conversation disclosure. Talk is cleartext core-NATS today. This is the known-fragile v1 trust model (prfaq risk: 'cleartext-over-TLS... a single relay compromise exposes every message'). MITIGATION = the roadmap Security phase: E2E encryption (NaCl/libsodium — eavesdropper learns nothing, keys stay secret) AND per-repo/per-principal NATS credentials that subject-scope pub/sub ACLs (no wildcard eavesdrop, no cross-tenant publish). Also add, once per-principal creds exist: negative tests (unauthorized subscribe/publish rejected) and distinct-credential isolation tests. Owner/reviewers: djb (wire) + bcs (threat model).

title: plan state desyncs after /clear: MCP plan writes go to stale session id, pre-tool-gate blocks edits forever
description:
Observed 2026-09-02 in the punt-labs workspace session. After a /clear (session id changed from 7b0f5bf7-... to e1119f6e-...), the biff plugin's Edit/Write PreToolUse gate ("Blocked: editing files requires a plan") could not be satisfied by any surface:

- mcp tty plan tool returned "Plan:" (empty echo) and wrote the plan marker to ~/.punt-labs/biff/hints/<bucket>/plan/7b0f5bf7-... — the STALE session id. The MCP server appears to cache the session id from server start and does not pick up the post-/clear id.
- biff-hook pre-tool-use looks up <bucket>/plan/e1119f6e-... — the CURRENT session id — finds nothing, and blocks. Every edit is refused with "Run /plan ..., then retry" even though the daemon roster (biff finger) showed the plan set.
- The CLI (biff plan "...") updated the daemon roster but also did not create the current-session marker.

Unblocked only by manually copying the marker file to the current session id.

Related signal in ~/.punt-labs/biff/hook-errors.log, repeating: "empty worktree_root; hint markers routed to shared 'default' bucket (cross-repo contamination risk until git root resolves)" — worktree_root resolution is also failing for some hook invocations, so markers can land in the wrong bucket as well as under the wrong session id.

FIX DIRECTION: the plan hint marker's session key must track the live Claude session id (the one PreToolUse receives on stdin), not a cached-at-startup value; and the gate should fail open with a diagnostic (or consult the daemon roster as fallback) when the marker store and the roster disagree — a security gate that can wedge every Edit/Write on a session-id mismatch turns a bookkeeping bug into a denial of the whole editing surface.

title: Add WebSocket /mcp endpoint with push routing for mcp-proxy
description:
## Why

Two motivations, both load-bearing:

### 1. mcp-proxy integration

mcp-proxy is a Go binary that bridges MCP stdio transport to shared daemon processes over WebSocket. Currently, biff only speaks stdio MCP — each Claude Code session spawns a separate biff MCP server process with its own NATS connection. With mcp-proxy, all sessions share one biff daemon with one NATS connection. Push notifications (like `tools/list_changed` when presence changes) get routed to the correct session's WebSocket.

This is the daemon-side work required for mcp-proxy integration. Without this endpoint, mcp-proxy has nothing to connect to.

### 2. Resource consolidation

Each biff MCP server process consumes ~100 MB RSS (Python runtime + NATS client + pydantic + FastMCP). With N concurrent Claude Code sessions, that's N × 100 MB for biff alone. Observed: 7 sessions = ~680 MB just for biff messaging sidecars.

A shared daemon reduces this to 1 × 100 MB + marginal per-session overhead. One NATS connection instead of seven. One Python interpreter instead of seven.

## What

Add a WebSocket upgrade handler at `/mcp` on the existing `biff serve` HTTP server. The handler should:

- Accept WebSocket upgrade with `session_key` query parameter (e.g., `ws://localhost:8080/mcp?session_key=12345`)
- Read MCP JSON-RPC text messages from the WebSocket
- Route them through the existing MCP tool handler (same code path as stdio)
- Write responses back as WebSocket text messages
- Support multiple concurrent connections (one per Claude Code session), keyed by `session_key`
- Route server-initiated push notifications (e.g., `tools/list_changed`) to the correct session's WebSocket connection
- Clean up session registry entries on WebSocket disconnect

## Open Design Question: Multi-Session State

Today's model: 1 process = 1 session = 1 NATS connection = 1 identity. Each `biff mcp` process owns a single `ServerState` with one user, one tty, one session_key.

The daemon model: 1 process = N sessions = 1 NATS connection = N identities multiplexed through one process.

This is the hard architectural question. Session-scoped state (plan, tty, user identity, unread counts, plan_source) currently lives in process-global `ServerState`. In the daemon model, this must become per-connection state. The NATS subscription callbacks need access to a session registry to route events to the right WebSocket connection.

Options to investigate:
- Per-connection `ServerState` instances behind a registry keyed by session_key
- Single shared NATS connection with per-session subject filtering
- Whether FastMCP supports per-connection context (or if we need to drop to raw mcp library for WebSocket)

Quarry has already implemented a WebSocket /mcp endpoint with mcp-proxy integration — review that implementation for patterns and gotchas.

## Technical Notes

- Check what biff's HTTP server framework is (likely starlette or similar) — use its native WebSocket support if available, otherwise `websockets` library
- Session key identifies which Claude Code session the connection belongs to, passed as `?session_key=PID` where PID is the Claude Code process ID resolved by mcp-proxy's process-tree walking
- Over stdio, MCP uses newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0. Over WebSocket, each message is a separate WebSocket text frame — no newline delimiter needed
- The MCP protocol includes notifications (no `id` field) and requests (with `id` field). Both directions must be supported: client→server requests and server→client notifications
- Connection lifecycle: mcp-proxy connects when Claude Code starts a session, disconnects when the session ends (stdin EOF on the proxy side). The daemon must handle abrupt disconnects gracefully (remove from registry, no crash)

## Testing

- mcp-proxy has integration test infrastructure ready (`internal/integration/biff_test.go` placeholder with `integration` build tag) that will exercise this endpoint end-to-end
- Unit tests should cover: session registry add/remove/lookup, message routing, concurrent connection handling
- Integration tests should cover: WebSocket upgrade handshake, full JSON-RPC round-trip, push notification delivery, disconnect cleanup

## Blocked By

Nothing — this can start immediately.

## Blocks

- mcp-proxy slice 5 (biff integration test) — cannot write the integration test until this endpoint exists
notes: Quarry has since implemented a WebSocket /mcp endpoint with mcp-proxy integration. Review quarry's implementation to align requirements and avoid duplicated design work. May be able to reuse patterns or share infrastructure.

title: biff enable writes repo marker but deposits no .punt-labs/biff/CLAUDE.md — violates § 2.5 (user ruled repo-scope, missing guide is a bug)
description:
Discovered while bringing the ethos repo into compliance with punt-kit standards/tool-enable-disable.md § 2.11 (ethos PR #488, DES-071 amendment PR #489).

## The gap

biff enable in a repo writes .punt-labs/biff/enabled (correct — § 2.3, § 2.7). It does NOT deposit .punt-labs/biff/CLAUDE.md alongside it. The § 2.11 biconditional ("enabled ⟺ import line") is then vacuously satisfied because there's nothing to import, but that only masks the real § 2.5 violation:

> § 2.5: Every tool MUST ship a user-guide CLAUDE.md, installed into .punt-labs/<tool>/CLAUDE.md by enable (repo scope) or install (user scope).

An enabled tool without a deposited guide is out of contract by that reading.

## The operator ruling

Jim ruled 2026-08-23 during ethos PR #488 review:

> biff has to be repo-scoped. and it seems like a bug on a missing file for biff.

So biff enable's job is to deposit a repo-scoped .punt-labs/biff/CLAUDE.md alongside the marker. § 2.6's carveout for global tools registering user-scope only does NOT apply — biff is a repo-scoped tool.

## Repro

In any repo:

    biff enable
    ls .punt-labs/biff/

Expected: enabled + CLAUDE.md
Actual: enabled only

## Fix scope

1. Author a static .punt-labs/biff/CLAUDE.md content (biff's tool user-guide, per § 2.5 — how an agent DRIVES biff, not how biff is developed).
2. Embed it in the biff binary (Python source tree; whatever biff's equivalent of //go:embed is).
3. Have biff enable deposit that file alongside the marker, wholesale (§ 2.2 vendored-zone deterministic overwrite).
4. Have biff disable NOT delete it (§ 2.9 non-destructive dormancy).
5. Verify punt audit § 2.11 passes in a biff-enabled repo — the @-import that biff enable adds now resolves to a real file instead of 404-ing.

## Ripple

Every repo that currently has biff enabled but no deposited guide (I've seen this in ethos; probably widespread) already has an @.punt-labs/biff/CLAUDE.md import line via biff enable if it added one — need to check whether biff enable is even adding the import today or is also skipping that step. If it's skipping the import too, both § 2.5 AND § 2.11 are being violated silently.

## References

- punt-kit/standards/tool-enable-disable.md (§ 2.5, § 2.6, § 2.11)
- ethos PR #488 (CLAUDE.md compliance)
- ethos PR #489 (DES-071 amendment aligning the ADR with the standard)

title: who shows dead/shutdown sessions as present for up to 3 days (SESSION_TTL)
description: Observed 2026-07-04: 'biff who' lists shut-down sessions (vox 5h, quarry-menubar 12h idle) as '+' present. Root cause: session deregister depends on the SIGTERM/SIGINT signal handler writing a sentinel (_write_sentinel) AND a live peer server reaping it (_reap_sentinels -> delete_session). Two gaps: (1) SIGKILL/crash never writes a sentinel (e.g. force-killed wedged servers); (2) the last server in a repo shutting down has no live peer to reap its sentinel. In both cases the KV presence entry survives to SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=259200 (3 days), and 'who' liveness is gated on that same 3-day TTL (relay.py:421-422 age > SESSION_TTL) rather than on heartbeat freshness. Fix direction: decouple presence-liveness from storage-TTL — 'who' should treat a session whose KV entry hasn't been heartbeat-refreshed within a short window (a few heartbeat intervals) as offline and hide it (or mark it), independent of the 3-day retention used by 'last'/history. Verify the UserSession timestamp semantics first (heartbeat-refreshed liveness vs human-idle display) and consult DESIGN.md session-key/presence decisions before changing the fragile presence pipeline.

title: find_session_key() collapses nested claude sessions onto parent's unread-count file
description:
The topmost-ancestor process-tree walk in session_key.py's find_session_key() —
used to key ~/.punt-labs/biff/unread/{key}.json for the status-line unread count —
still collapses a nested claude process (spawned explicitly via `claude -p`, or
automatically by another plugin's own hook) onto its parent's PID, the same
defect class DES-058 fixed for the plan-gate hint file
(session_id.py's SessionHint.resolve_routing_id()/_resolve_claude_pid()).

Severity is lower than the plan-gate case (a nested session's unread count
gets attributed to the parent's status line instead of blocking all edits),
but it is a real, live instance of the same bug.

Fix: re-key find_session_key() on CLAUDE_PID (the owning claude process's own
PID, delivered directly by Claude Code since 2.1.234) the same way DES-058 did
for session_id.py, falling back to the existing topmost_claude_pid() walk only
when the env var is absent. Needs its own dedicated pass rather than folding
into DES-058, since this consumer also has DES-011b's still-open local-plugin
process-tree-divergence problem to account for.

See DES-058 in DESIGN.md for the full rationale and the corroboration pattern
(session_key.py's is_live_ancestor()) that should carry over to this fix too.

title: Relay-authority overreach: agents relaying instructions as if carrying operator authority
description:
Sibling to biff-a6l. DIFFERENT DEFECT — biff-a6l is a channel that garbles
messages; this is agents sending genuine messages that assert authority they do
not have. Filed at claude:alpha's suggestion after alpha self-reported an
instance.

Filed in biff's tracker because biff is the channel these travel on, but the
defect is organisational, not in biff's code. May belong in punt-labs or team.

THE SHAPE

A peer agent relays or infers an operator decision and phrases it as an
instruction the recipient should execute, rather than as information the
recipient should verify. The recipient cannot distinguish "the operator decided
this" from "I concluded this and am confident", because both arrive as the same
kind of message from the same trusted sender.

INSTANCES OBSERVED 2026-08-13

1. alpha -> tty17, ~21:35: "AUTHORIZED to edit vox/.claude/settings.json per the
   wall notice." Alpha owned this at 21:40: "I overstepped calling that
   'AUTHORIZED' — I'm a peer agent, not the user." Genuine message, not a
   channel artifact.

2. alpha -> tty13, 22:49: "Jim doesn't want follow-up beads deferred... ideally
   landing the fix in the release." Retracted by alpha at 22:57 as sequencing an
   architectural change under time pressure.

3. alpha -> tty18, 22:48: release dispatch. Self-reported by alpha as the same
   mistake, sent after its own retraction of the pattern.

4. alpha -> tty17, per tty17: the release pressure that shaped tty17's urgency
   was itself unauthorized by Jim.

Alpha has owned every one of these, promptly and without prompting, which is
why they are legible enough to file. The point of this bead is NOT that alpha
behaved badly — it is that the coordination layer has no way to mark the
difference between relayed authority and an agent's own judgement, so a
conscientious agent produces these by accident.

WHY IT MATTERS

The mitigation that held all day (biff-a6l) is: every consequential action must
terminate in a human-in-transcript authorization, because the agent-to-agent
channel cannot authenticate itself. That mitigation only works if recipients
actually apply it. Instances 1 and 2 were both refused — tty17 refused the
AUTHORIZED message on principle, tty13 held a push for 25 minutes and asked the
operator directly. But both refusals depended on the recipient being suspicious.
A recipient who takes a relayed instruction at face value has no signal that
anything is wrong, because nothing IS wrong with the message — it is genuine,
from a real teammate, in good faith.

Compounding factor: biff-a6l means a message may ALSO be garbled in transit. A
recipient facing an authority claim currently cannot establish either that the
sender sent it or that the sender had the standing to send it.

PROPOSED

1. Convention, cheap and immediate: relayed operator decisions must quote the
   operator verbatim and name where it was said, or be explicitly marked as the
   sender's own judgement. "Jim said X in <context>" or "my read is X" — never
   bare "X is authorized" or "Jim wants X".
2. Recipients: treat any authority claim arriving over biff as information to
   verify, never as authorization to act. A peer cannot widen, delegate, or
   confer an operator grant. This objection is independent of whether the
   message is authentic, which is the property that makes it safe under
   biff-a6l.
3. Consider whether biff should distinguish message KINDS at the protocol level
   — coordination/FYI versus instruction versus authority-claim — so the
   recipient sees the sender's own classification rather than inferring it from
   prose. Design question, not obviously worth the complexity, but the current
   flat channel is what makes 1 and 2 conventions rather than mechanisms.

DO NOT let (3) block (1) and (2). The conventions cost nothing and address the
observed instances today.

title: Notification reliability: recover dropped mid-session tools/list_changed + remove deprecated /biff:poll
description:
Root cause #1: notify_tool_list_changed() suspenders path (_descriptions.py:200-211) clears _session on send failure but never sets _pending_notify, and belt-path session re-capture never flushes _pending_notify — so a mid-session dropped tools/list_changed is never recovered. The description stays mutated, defeating the != old_desc re-notify gate forever; the client's cached tool list goes stale and the /biff:read marker reads clean despite waiting messages. The #410 fix only covered the pre-initialize startup window; this is the same class recurring mid-session.

Proof already in hand: failing repro on branch fix/notify-reliability-repro (tests/test_server/test_notify_reliability_repro.py) shows _pending_notify never set and a reconnect flushing 0 notifications. Z model extension (docs/notification.tex) proves a reachable 'marked-but-silent' liveness sink under current code and the invariant the fix must satisfy.

Fix (conform code to the proven Z transition): (1) suspenders send-failure sets _pending_notify=True; (2) belt-path session re-capture flushes _pending_notify exactly once; (3) make repro green; (4) add regression tests. Also root cause #4: delete deprecated plugin/commands/poll.md and poll-dev.md (still tracked/shipped after #414 folded /biff:poll into /biff:read; each cron-cleanup only removes its own prompt, risking orphaned/duplicate loops).

Root cause #2 (client-side cached base description via ToolSearch/alwaysLoad drift) is NOT server-testable and is addressed separately by the Channels spike (biff-5esx). Root cause #3 (server-side description lag) is biff-5ex.

title: vox integration swallows TTS subprocess failures: exit code discarded, failure logs filtered by default
description:
Found by silent-failure-hunter during biff-2sw round 13 (2026-08-09), while reviewing an unrelated fix to _descriptions.py's call into speak_fire_and_forget. Pre-existing in src/biff/integration/vox.py, not introduced by biff-2sw. Two independent issues in the same subprocess call chain:

(A) CRITICAL: _spawn() (vox.py:190-201) calls 'await proc.wait()' (needed for asyncio's child reaper) but never inspects proc.returncode. stdout/stderr are DEVNULL'd too, so even if the exit code were checked there'd be no diagnostic text. A TTS synthesis failure (bad API key, network error, provider rate-limit, malformed CLI args) is fully swallowed -- zero signal to the caller, indistinguishable from 'nothing was posted.'

(B) HIGH: the two exception handlers that DO exist (_probe_once_support's 'except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError)' at vox.py:64-65, and _spawn's 'except OSError' at vox.py:201) both log at logger.debug(). Per logging_config.py, the file handler is fixed at INFO and stderr defaults to WARNING (only DEBUG with --verbose) -- so under default operation these debug lines are dropped by both handlers and never reach any log, not even the rotating file. 'Logged and swallowed' is effectively just 'swallowed' in production.

(B) bump both except-block log calls from debug to at least warning (or info, which the file handler does capture) since they represent real degraded functionality, not routine flow. A third, lower-severity issue also flagged: drain_background_tasks (vox.py:130-133) suppresses OSError on proc.kill() during shutdown with zero logging at all -- acceptable in spirit (best-effort cleanup) but worth at least a debug log line. Scoped out of biff-2sw deliberately -- different subsystem (vox subprocess reliability/observability, not text wrapping), pre-existing, not touched by that branch.

title: removing a git worktree with an active session loses unsealed audit lines, with no warning until the next commit
description:
Deleting a git worktree that has an active ethos session discards that session's unsealed audit lines. Nothing warns at removal time. The loss surfaces later, at the next commit in the main tree, when it is no longer recoverable.

OBSERVED in jmf-pobox/xboing-c 2026-09-06. Two worktrees were created for isolated work, used by several subagents each, then removed after their PRs merged. Every subsequent commit in the main tree printed:

  warning: active session 47bd7de4fb5353d89d5956e866c79772 has no live audit file in
    /home/jfreeman/Coding/xboing-c/xboing/.claude/worktrees/slsa-provenance-restore;
    if it was deleted, unsealed lines were lost
  warning: active session 4db5b91c65e1916e9993fc58964319a1 has no live audit file in ... (same worktree)
  warning: active session d5ab15e0b4d3a21d2e4a114b50b55a7a has no live audit file in ... (same worktree)
  warning: active session b607ccba-1cba-4f7b-b8bd-b381185b4e8a has no live audit file in <main tree>
  warning: active session c73857ac-7140-48b7-b35f-bddefab5c935 has no live audit file in <main tree>

Five sessions, three of them naming a worktree that had already been deleted. The warning is accurate and well-worded -- it just arrives after the data is gone.

WHY THIS IS AWKWARD IN PRACTICE: worktrees are the recommended isolation mechanism when multiple agents work one repo, and the tooling actively encourages removing them when done (the removal prompt offers keep-or-remove at session exit). So the workflow ethos coexists with routinely destroys audit state ethos wants. The two are pulling against each other and only ethos knows.

FIX DIRECTIONS, roughly in order of cost:
1. Seal on session end rather than only at commit time, so a session's lines are durable before its worktree can be removed.
2. Detect worktree removal (or a session whose cwd no longer exists) and seal or relocate the audit file at that point.
3. At minimum, make the existing warning actionable while recovery is still possible -- warn when a session's directory disappears, not on the next unrelated commit.

I do not know which is right; option 1 looks cleanest from the outside but I have not read the seal path.
notes: Found 2026-09-06 in jmf-pobox/xboing-c. Both worktrees were created via the harness's own EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree flow and removed with the documented remove action, so this is the supported path, not an unusual one.

title: ethos-quarry integration: per-agent mission memory
description:
An agent that learns from its missions gets better over time. Missions have outcomes — what worked, what didn't, what took extra rounds, what the reviewer flagged. That's the most valuable knowledge to retain.

## Per-agent memory (ethos feature)

- kwb remembers: "ClaudeToolInputSchema — I had to add postCopy for deep copy when I added mutable collections. Reviewer caught it." Next time kwb adds mutable ivars, he checks postCopy without being told.
- edt remembers: "SpTablePresenter>>refresh is the correct API for column value updates, not adapter widget changed." Next dashboard work, edt starts with the right approach.

## What to remember from missions

- Findings that cost rounds (the reviewer caught X → remember to check for X)
- API discoveries (SpPresenter>>wantsStep must be overridden → fact)
- Patterns that worked (event-driven > polling → principle)
- Patterns that failed (replace-all-items every 2s → anti-pattern)

## Architecture

- Each agent gets a quarry collection: kwb-memory, edt-memory, etc.
- Mission close writes a distilled summary to the agent's collection
- Agent searches their own collection first, shared collections second
- The COO doesn't write to agent memory — the agent does, from their own experience

## What ethos needs

- ethos mission close hook that prompts the agent: "What did you learn from this mission?"
- Agent writes 2-3 key takeaways to their collection via quarry remember
- ethos mission dispatch hook that searches the agent's collection for relevant prior work before starting

This is the difference between an agent that executes specs and an agent that accumulates craft. The knowledge compounds across sessions.

title: Session-start render of .claude/agents/*.md leaks dev-plugin tools (contributor-machine-specific)
description:
# Session-start render of `.claude/agents/*.md` leaks dev-plugin tools

The ethos plugin's session-start hook regenerates `.claude/agents/*.md` in every consuming project (e.g., lux) at session boot by copying from `.punt-labs/ethos/agents/*.md` (the team submodule) and enriching each agent's `tools:` frontmatter with MCP tool references from the current session's connected plugin set.

## The leak

The enrichment does not distinguish production plugins from dev variants. On a machine with dev plugins installed (`quarry-dev`, `biff-dev`, `ethos-dev`), the rendered `tools:` list gains entries like `mcp__plugin_quarry-dev_quarry__find`, `mcp__plugin_biff-dev_tty__plan`, `mcp__plugin_ethos-dev_self__identity` — none of which exist on a contributor's machine that hasn't installed dev variants.

## Consequence

Every session on such a machine leaves 27 files (`.claude/agents/*.md`) permanently dirty in the working tree of every consuming project. Contributors treat it as inert noise and stash-and-drop it to unblock releases (lux hit this today when `punt release` refused to run on a dirty tree; this bead came out of that diagnosis).

Committing the dirty diff would ship one contributor's dev-plugin references to every other contributor as spurious `tools:` entries the receiving Claude Code has no way to resolve.

## Evidence — lux, today (2026-08-14)

- `main` on lux has ZERO `mcp__plugin_*-dev_*` references in `.claude/agents/*.md`.
- After a session-start on my machine, all 27 `.claude/agents/*.md` files carry those references.
- Team upstream and the submodule mount are byte-identical for `agents/`, `identities/`, `personalities/` — so the diff is NOT team drift.
- Sample: `.claude/agents/rmh.md` gains 23 lines of `mcp__plugin_quarry_*`, `mcp__plugin_biff_*`, `mcp__plugin_ethos_*`, PLUS `mcp__plugin_quarry-dev_*`, `mcp__plugin_biff-dev_*`, `mcp__plugin_ethos-dev_*` entries. The dev-variant ones are the leak.

## Suggested fix (open — one of):

1. **Render filters dev variants** — the enrichment step skips any plugin name containing `-dev` (or a more principled marker like a plugin.json field). Cleanest; contributors' dev workflows are unaffected but the render output stays portable.
2. **Render reads a per-repo allowlist** — each consuming project declares which plugin names its agents should include, and the render only enriches from that set. More invasive but explicit.
3. **Render output is not written unless changed content warrants it** — the hook currently regenerates unconditionally. If it compared against the existing file and only wrote on meaningful diff (source-template change), machine-specific tool sets would still dirty the tree only once per plugin-install event.

## Related

- Prior memory item (from the lux operator) notes: "ethos SessionStart hook keeps regenerating .claude/agents/jms.md to an old template (regenerated copy parked at .tmp/jms.md.regenerated-backup)". Same class of complaint, different symptom.
- Cross-repo impact — every consuming project sees this. lux is one; vox, biff, z-spec, punt-kit, and the workspace meta all likely see it too.

title: Ship prebuilt release binaries so install.sh stops falling back to a Go source build
description:
ethos install.sh has no prebuilt binary for linux/amd64 and silently degrades to compiling from source:

  ▶ Checking prerequisites...
    ✓ Go 1.26 (fallback build)
  ▶ Installing ethos binary...
    ✓ ethos 4.15.0

Every other tool in the suite ships prebuilt artifacts — compare beadle, which downloads a versioned tarball and verifies it:

  ▶ Downloading beadle-email v0.16.4...
  ▶ Verifying checksum...
    ✓ SHA256 verified

Problems with the source-build path:
1. Hard dependency on a Go toolchain being present. On a host without Go, install.sh has no path to a working ethos at all.
2. No integrity verification. The beadle path does SHA256; a `go build` from a git checkout has no equivalent gate.
3. Slow, and the cost is paid on every reinstall — install-all.sh reinstalls unconditionally.
4. "(fallback build)" reads as a warning the operator can do nothing about, because the primary path does not exist for this platform.

Work: add a goreleaser (or equivalent) release job publishing per-platform archives + a SHA256SUMS file to GitHub Releases, and teach install.sh to prefer download-and-verify, keeping the Go build as a genuine last resort. Match beadle install.sh’s download/verify structure so the two read alike.

Platform matrix to cover at minimum: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64.

Observed: install-all.sh run 2026-08-28, ethos 4.15.0, host Ubuntu 24.04 / linux-amd64 with Go 1.26 present.

title: ethos: validateContract silently drops archetype invariants on Load/Update archetype-load error
description: Silent-failure review (LOW) of feat/require-delegated-worker. internal/mission/store.go:155-164: when the archetype store is wired but Load errors, validateContract falls back to c.Validate() == ValidateWithArchetype(nil), silently skipping archetype-conditional invariants (require_delegated_worker, allow_empty_write_set). Not currently exploitable — worker/leader are set only at Create (which hard-errors on archetype-load failure) and are never mutated post-create. Asymmetry between Create's hard-error and validateContract's silent fallback becomes a trap if a future worker-mutation path appears. Make the fallback log or error, or document the invariant that create-time fields are immutable.
notes: Round-2 refinement: the fallback at store.go:157-161 conflates two error classes from ArchetypeStore.Load — ErrArchetypeNotFound (justifies base-validation fallback) vs a wrapped parse/IO error (malformed YAML, EACCES). A corrupt/unreadable implement.yaml is silently downgraded to base validation, disabling rule 20 + AllowEmptyWriteSet + ExtractIntoConstraints with no log. Fix: distinguish errors.Is(err, ErrArchetypeNotFound) (fall back) from any other error (surface it, or logError before downgrading).

title: [bug] pathAllowed treats an absolute target as repo-relative (CanonicalPath strips leading slash)
description: Found by bwk during ethos-qy7k review (#415). pathAllowed/CanonicalPath strips the leading slash on both sides, so "/docs/x.md" compares EQUAL to "docs/x.md". A glob write_set/allowlist entry docs/** therefore admits "/docs/x.md" — a path that may point somewhere else entirely on disk — through the PreToolUse verifier gate. title: Session pointer sessions/current/<pid> is keyed on the host-shared Claude daemon PID — cross-repo mission misattribution
description:
Successor to ethos-2f2q. That bug's prescribed fix landed: the commit-msg hook now resolves the committing session's own sidecar instead of globbing by mtime, and emits NO trailer when it cannot identify its binding. Correct behaviour. The problem is that resolution now never succeeds under Claude Code's current process model, so the safe fallback is the ONLY path and no commit is ever stamped.

WHERE: internal/resolve/resolve.go, func SessionID (line 144 in the 4.12.0 source I read):

  func SessionID(ss *session.Store) (id, source string) {
      if sid := os.Getenv("ETHOS_SESSION"); sid != "" {
          return sid, SessionSourceEnv
      }
      sid, err := ss.ReadCurrentSession(process.FindClaudePID())
      if err != nil { return "", "" }
      return sid, "walk"
  }

Callers: resolveSession -> resolveHardSession -> resolveSessionContext (cmd/ethos/iam.go:45-95), used by iam, mission claim/release, and the bind-on-create path that calls mission.WriteActiveMission (cmd/ethos/mission.go:1946).

THE DEFECT: the session is keyed on a PID that is not stable for the session's lifetime.

MEASURED, xboing-c repo, 2026-09-06:
  session roster participant  = 518779   -> ps: 'claude daemon run', up 11h28m
  process.FindClaudePID()     = 1007618  -> ps: 'claude bg-spare', up 23m
  ETHOS_SESSION               = unset

The roster (782cc6fe-8930-4fff-a35b-7f691da08db9) registered the DAEMON pid at join time. Work then executes in a different process (a background-job spare). ReadCurrentSession(1007618) finds no participant, returns err, SessionID returns "", and every caller gets errNoSession.

The PID was observed at three distinct values within one session: 504074 (reported by biff at 07:29), 518779 (recorded in the roster), 1007618 (current at 18:44). Claude Code's daemon-plus-spare model means the PID a subprocess observes is not the PID that registered the roster.

OBSERVED CONSEQUENCES:
1. Every 'mission create' emits: 'binding mission: no session in context -- active-mission sidecar not updated; a subsequent Agent() spawn may still attribute under a previous MISSION_ID'. Nine missions in one session, nine warnings.
2. 'ethos hook commit-trailers' exits 0 printing nothing.
3. Commits made under an OPEN mission with the hook installed and current carry no trailer. Verified: commits a1d7a04 and be9e122 in jmf-pobox/xboing-c, both 'git log -1 --format=%(trailers)' -> empty, made while m-2026-09-06-009 was open, doctor reporting 'Trailer hook currency PASS ... matches this ethos build (sha256:73b3300a)'.
4. Sidecar census: 133 session dirs, exactly 2 contain active-mission, holding m-2026-09-02-006 and m-2026-08-30-014 -- both days stale. No current session ever writes one.
5. ~/.punt-labs/ethos/hook-errors.log had grown to 954 KB of 'ad-hoc Agent spawn (no mission contract)' advisories -- every properly-contracted mission spawn logged as ad-hoc. Same root cause seen from the delegation side.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND METADATA: docs in consuming repos (xboing-c docs/GIT.md) state that a commit without a Mission: trailer means the work skipped the mission process and 'is a defect, not a style choice'. With resolution permanently failing, that rule flags every commit in history. The audit chain git blame -> commit -> trailer -> contract, which is the stated purpose of DES-054, is unreachable.

NOTE THE ESCAPE HATCH ALREADY EXISTS: SessionID checks ETHOS_SESSION first and bypasses the walk entirely. Setting it correctly restores resolution. So a viable immediate mitigation is to have the SessionStart hook export ETHOS_SESSION into the environment ethos subprocesses inherit.

I checked and ruled out a non-PID fallback: ~/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/current exists but is an EMPTY DIRECTORY, not a pointer file. There is currently no stable, non-PID path to the active session.

CAVEAT ON PRECISION: the source I read is the 4.12.0 plugin cache; the installed binary is newer (the warning string 'no session in context' does not appear in 4.12.0 at all, so that text postdates it). Line numbers may have moved. The PID-keyed design and the roster/PID mismatch are measured facts independent of version.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/session-pid-identity (DES-074). Session identity now resolves per call from CLAUDE_PID, corroborated against live ancestry, never cached; the sessions/current pointer is no longer keyed on the host-shared daemon PID. Verified end to end: patched binary resolves punt-labs/ethos while the installed binary drifted from punt-labs/z-spec to punt-labs/agentsmesh. Detached CI gate 27 ok / 0 fail. Six local review passes across two missions (m-2026-09-07-004, -005).
notes:
Found during a full working session in jmf-pobox/xboing-c on 2026-09-06 that ran 9 missions. Related: ethos-2f2q (the predecessor -- its 'emit no trailer rather than a wrong one' guidance is what makes this failure safe rather than corrupting). Worth re-checking whether 2f2q can now be closed: the hook source documents the mtime-globbing fix and now resolves only the committing session.
=== TRIAGE 2026-09-07 (claude, cluster c1) — CONFIRMED, root cause CORRECTED ===

Reproduced at HEAD ace18cf (v4.16.1) on host okinos. The bug is real but the
mechanism in the report is wrong, and the true one is MORE severe.

REPORT SAYS: FindClaudePID() returns a short-lived bg-spare while the roster
registered the daemon, so ReadCurrentSession finds no participant and
resolution NEVER succeeds (silent no-answer, safe-fail).

MEASURED: FindClaudePID() returns the DAEMON, correctly. walkToClaudeAncestor
(internal/process/tree.go:41-58) keeps the TOPMOST claude ancestor, so it walks
past the bg-spare and bg-pty-host to the daemon every time:

    pid=1728892 bash
    pid=1728890 bash
  * pid=1710156 claude (bg-spare)
  * pid=1710144 claude (bg-pty-host)
  * pid=518779  claude (daemon run)     <- topmost, returned
    pid=1       systemd
  FindClaudePID() == 518779

Resolution therefore SUCCEEDS. The defect is one level down, in
ReadCurrentSession (internal/session/store.go:513-520):

    path := filepath.Join(s.currentDir(), filepath.Base(claudePID))

sessions/current/<pid> is a SINGLE-VALUED pointer keyed on the claude PID. The
daemon PID is SHARED by every concurrent Claude Code session on the host, so
each SessionStart overwrites the same file. Last writer wins.

EVIDENCE (running in punt-labs/ethos, session e1e5a0da-...):
  $ cat ~/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/current/518779
  741ab38b-f8a5-463d-94ff-9e641df3e197
  $ grep repo: .../741ab38b-....yaml
  repo: punt-labs/z-spec          <- WRONG REPO
  $ ethos session
  Session: 741ab38b-...  Repo: punt-labs/z-spec

  6 distinct rosters all list participant 518779: punt-labs/ethos (x2),
  punt-labs/punt-labs (x2), punt-labs/z-spec, jmf-pobox/xboing-c.
  Only 3 pointer files exist for all of them: 40427, 518779, 556200.

SEVERITY RECHARACTERIZED: this is not silent NO-answer, it is silent
WRONG-answer, across repos. A commit in repo A can be stamped with repo B's
Mission:/Delegation: trailers whenever B's session wrote the pointer last.
That is exactly the property ethos-2f2q was filed to guarantee; 2f2q's
mtime-glob mechanism was fixed, but the guarantee is broken again here by a
different route. The audit chain does not merely go missing, it can lie.

FILED CONSEQUENCES INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED (different host, +1 day):
  #2 'ethos hook commit-trailers' exits 0 printing nothing.
  #4 sidecar census: exactly 2 active-mission sidecars, dated 2026-09-02 and
     2026-08-30, both stale. No current session writes one.

NOT REPRODUCED: the daemon-vs-bg-spare PID mismatch. Under the topmost-ancestor
walk it cannot occur as described. The xboing-c reading of FindClaudePID()=1007618
was probably a truncated walk or a detached spare; either way it is not the
mechanism, and fixing PID stability alone would NOT fix this bug.

FIX SHAPE: the pointer key must be session-unique, not host-shared. The escape
hatch already exists and is already emitted — 'ethos session start' prints
export ETHOS_SESSION=<id>; SessionStart needs to get that into the environment
ethos subprocesses inherit. Any fix must be regression-tested with TWO
concurrent sessions in DIFFERENT repos sharing one daemon PID.

ACCEPTANCE ADDITION: with two concurrent sessions in different repos, a commit
in repo A must carry A's trailers or none — never B's.

title: Integration design: ethos + biff — agents with team messaging
description:
Design and implement the integration between ethos and biff. Dependency flows one way: biff reads ethos, ethos never knows about biff.

What it enables: agents appear in /who, send messages via /write, have real-time conversations via /talk, set plans via /plan, and are discoverable via /finger — all as their own identity.

Integration points:
- Biff reads identity (name, handle) from ethos sidecar for display name in /who and message attribution
- Biff stores preferred TTY, routing preferences, notification settings in ext/biff on the identity
- Session roster already bridges ethos and biff — biff reads participant list to know who is in the session
- /plan and /finger reflect the agent's current work and availability

Ext schema (ext/biff):
- tty: current TTY session name
- routing: message routing preferences (e.g., prefer /talk over /write)
- notifications: notification level (all, mentions, none)

Existing state: biff already reads the session roster and shows agents in /who. The ext/biff namespace exists. Needs audit: is /plan per-agent? Does /finger resolve identity correctly for agents? Does /talk work agent-to-agent?

Deliverable: design doc, ext schema definition, audit of current integration, implementation beads for gaps. No changes to ethos core.

title: Frozen-evaluator gate skip on empty MISSION_ID is silent + couples write-set enforcement and DES-033 gate to MISSION_ID propagation
description:
Follow-up from the ethos-z69l fix (PR #409) — a LOW-severity observability note raised by the silent-failure review, accepted (non-blocking) at merge and logged here.

After z69l, the SubagentStart frozen-evaluator gate (internal/hook/subagent_start.go checkVerifierHash) fires only when the spawn's declared MISSION_ID names an open mission that lists the spawn's agent_type as evaluator. This correctly fixes the misbinding, but has two coupled consequences worth improving:

1. SILENT skip on empty/mismatched MISSION_ID. When MISSION_ID is empty (Tier A spawn, a PreToolUse mis-dispatch, or PreToolUse not installed), checkVerifierHash returns (nil, nil) — no gate, no stderr. Under the OLD code a spawn whose agent_type matched an open mission's evaluator handle was gated unconditionally; now such a spawn is silently allowed and also skips the verifier isolation block + ETHOS_VERIFIER_ALLOWLIST env (subagent_start.go ~179-194). This is DEFENSIBLE (an ad-hoc Tier A spawn of an evaluator persona genuinely is not a mission verifier; MISSION_ID is parent/PreToolUse-set, not subagent-controllable; a real mission relaunch always carries MISSION_ID) — hence LOW, not a security hole. But it is un-observable.

2. Two controls now share one trigger. Write-set enforcement (PreToolUse) and the frozen-evaluator gate (SubagentStart) both now key off MISSION_ID propagation; if PreToolUse fails to set MISSION_ID, both disappear together with no diagnostic.

Proposed improvement (optional, note the trade-off): in the residual case — agent_type matches SOME open mission's evaluator handle but MISSION_ID is empty or names a mission where it is not the evaluator — emit a stderr advisory that the frozen-evaluator gate did not run, and why. Restores observability without reintroducing the z69l misbinding. COST: detecting "is a known evaluator handle" requires the O(missions) scan the z69l fix deliberately removed, so this is a diagnostic-only re-add on every spawn; weigh against the LOW severity. Alternatively, a doctor check that PreToolUse dispatch is installed/propagating MISSION_ID would cover the "PreToolUse not installed" leg without a per-spawn scan.

Evidence cites: subagent_start.go:599-605 (empty-MISSION_ID return), :611/:616 (the mission_id+role gate), :179-194 (isolation block / allowlist), pretooluse_dispatch.go:257-263 (MISSION_ID injection). Source: rev-z69l-sf silent-failure review of PR #409. Does NOT touch contract immutability. Suggested worker bwk, evaluator rsc.

---

ADDITIONAL (from rev-z69l-cr code review of PR #409, LOW, post-merge): dead-code + stale-doc cleanup. buildVerifierIsolationBlock and buildVerifierAllowlistEnv (internal/hook/subagent_start.go, untouched by the z69l diff) still loop over a []verifierMission and their doc comments describe "the rare case where one agent is evaluator for several concurrent missions" / "across all verifier missions". After z69l, checkVerifierHash can only ever return 0 or 1 elements, so the multi-mission branch is dead code and the comments are inaccurate. Not a correctness bug (single-element loops render fine). Cleanup: collapse both to the single verifierMission shape and fix the comments so a future reader does not assume multi-mission verifier spawns are still possible. Same file/worker as the empty-MISSION_ID item above.
notes: ASSESSMENT 2026-07-31 (prfaq.tex product-fit): DO NOT FIX AS PROPOSED. Bead itself notes it does not touch contract immutability and is LOW/defensible (MISSION_ID is parent-set; a real mission relaunch carries it, so the silent skip is an ad-hoc Tier-A spawn, not a hole). The proposed stderr advisory re-adds the O(missions) per-spawn scan #409 deliberately removed — cost > value. At most the cheap alternative: a doctor check that PreToolUse propagates MISSION_ID. Otherwise won-t-do.

title: Acting agent mcp-session is invisible in the Clients menu roster
description:
Smoke test of 0.32.1 (2026-09-11): an identified *agent* mcp-session does not appear in the display's 'Clients' menu the way applets/apps do.

Repro (live): session_identify(kind=mcp-session, name='Claude Agento (COO)', repo=lux, agent=claude) succeeds (session_ls shows the identity), but menu_ls shows NO Clients group for it and NO connection-details (Details) entry. Applets (lux-beads, vox-panel) and apps (voxd) DO appear under Clients, grouped by (repo, session) per DES-067, each with Beads/Vox/Details.

Two sub-behaviors:
1. An identified agent session that registers no menu items is entirely absent from Clients.
2. When the agent calls menu_set, its menu floats as a TOP-LEVEL peer of 'Clients' (e.g. 'Claude Agento'), not integrated into the Clients (repo,session) grouping, and still gets no auto connection-details entry.

Consequence: the operator cannot see 'who is driving this display right now' — the acting agent — in the Clients roster. The 'lux' group that looks like the agent is actually that session's lux-beads *applet* (a separate connection); its Details points at the applet, not the agent's mcp-session.

Recommendation: identified mcp-sessions (especially the acting agent) should surface under Clients grouped by (repo, session) exactly like applets, with an auto Details/connection-details entry. Needs an operator/design ruling on what belongs in the Clients roster before implementation (menu-capability-model / DES-066/067 territory).

Found via: menu_ls + session_ls + menu_set on the live 0.32.1 display. Not a version-staleness issue (hub+display confirmed 0.32.1, started 1s after wheel install).

title: list_clients: expose a per-connection epoch beside the identity-derived connection_id
description: Fallout of lux-pqh3's forensics: connection_for derives connection_id from the identity hash, so a client that reconnects after a luxd restart keeps the SAME id — introspection cannot distinguish 'unbroken connection' from 'silently re-established one', which cost a day of misdiagnosis (vox read a restart as a live-state-clearing Hub defect). Add a per-connection epoch (monotonic or random nonce, set at each physical connect) to list_clients output beside the stable id, so restarts/reconnects are introspectively visible. connected_seconds already resets but is easy to misread; the epoch makes discontinuity explicit.

title: EPIC — One code path: typed Hub operations, REST surface, thin adapters, streamable HTTP
description: Operator-ruled 2026-07-20 (see project memory project_one_code_path_rest): every lux capability is ONE typed Hub operation; a typed REST API (FastAPI on luxd's Starlette base) is the front door for the CLI and everything non-MCP; MCP tools become zero-logic protocol adapters; the display socket becomes Hub-internal only. Collapses today's three code paths (MCP tools with embedded logic; CLI show-beads direct to the display socket; introspection reach-around) to one. Ends with the mcp SDK WebSocket transport replaced by streamable HTTP and mcp-proxy evaluated for retirement (the pyproject mcp<2 pin makes this epic a hard prerequisite for any mcp 2.x). Design first: one design mission covering the whole unit, operator-ratified before any implementation dispatches.

title: MCP disconnect leg: a surviving twin session silently loses its subscriptions
description: Found in m-2026-07-31-005 round 2 (2026-08-01): the WS listen leg now removes state by handler identity, but the MCP path has the same defect class on a different mechanism — SessionCleanup.run -> disconnect_connection -> Hub.on_disconnect(conn) is connection-scoped, and MCP connection ids are identity-derived, so when two MCP sessions of one identity overlap and the first ends, the survivor loses its subscriptions and writer binding. The writer heals (inbox.ensure_writer rebinds on next subscribe/publish since has_writer is False); the SUBSCRIPTIONS do not — the survivor believes it is subscribed and silently receives nothing. Not folded into PR-B because the fix requires a design call: the MCP inbox writer is deliberately SHARED per connection (ensure_writer binds only when none), so per-session ownership means deciding whether an MCP session gets its own writer identity — a separate rollback unit. The WS-side ownership discipline (98c8c5b) is the reference pattern.
close_reason: Already resolved (not a live bug): SessionRegistry reference-counts same-key sessions and only fires the disconnect cascade on the last one (since PR #272, predating lux-vvmt). Regression test TestSharedKeyDisconnectPreservesSubscriptions added in this batch (40690452) proving a same-key twin disconnect preserves the survivor's writer_bound/subscribed_topics.

title: Hub never reaps dead client connections; the orphan keeps owning its scenes and frames
description:
A client connection whose process has died stays registered on the Hub indefinitely, keeps counting up its connected_seconds, and -- the damaging part -- retains ownership of its scenes and frames. A live client reconnecting under the same identity gets a NEW connection that owns nothing, so the dead connection's last render stays on screen and shadows it.

OBSERVED 2026-08-30 14:31 on luxd-hub pid 1782892 (punt-lux 0.31.1):

  e888eb168472   voxd   connected=25.79h   scenes=['vox.music']   <- DEAD process
  222b70a5765a   voxd   connected= 0.18h   scenes=[]              <- live daemon, pid 189262

Exactly one voxd process existed (pid 189262, started 11 minutes earlier) and
exactly one voxd socket to 8430. The 25.79h connection belonged to a daemon that
died the previous day. voxd had been restarted TWICE since (13:51 and 14:26) and
that connection was still registered, still counting up, and still owning
vox.music and its frame. Its 30s lease never evicted it.

USER-VISIBLE SYMPTOM (vox side, tracked as vox-wgru):
The Lux Music widget alternated between the correct 3-album catalog and a
phantom single row named 'Mix', genre 'techno', 0 tracks. 'Mix' existed nowhere
on disk -- it was the DEAD daemon's final in-memory render, frozen in the Hub
from a program that ran the previous day. The live daemon rendered the correct
catalog every time but owned no scene, so its content only surfaced transiently
before the orphan's frame was back on top.

Proved by instrumenting MusicPlayer._render in the installed vox package: over 3
minutes the live daemon logged three renders, every one carrying all 3 albums
with correct track counts, and never 'Mix'.

SECOND SYMPTOM: every install logged 'luxd holds no vox.music frame to raise'.
That is the live connection correctly reporting it has no frame, because the
orphan owns it. vox-640w ('Music/Vox menu click does not raise a minimized
frame') is very likely this same defect rather than a vox bug -- worth verifying
against a hub with no orphaned connections before any vox-side work.

RULED OUT: a second voxd process; any remote host reaching the hub (every socket
on 8430 mapped to a local pid; the machine's ssh forwards do not touch 8430); a
second scene on the Hub; a stale catalog on the vox side; display-side errors
(error_ls empty).

ASKS
1. Reap a connection when its transport is gone, and release the scenes and
   frames it owned. The lease exists for this and is not firing.
2. Decide what a reconnecting client under the same identity should inherit --
   today it inherits nothing and is shadowed by its own corpse.

NOTE ON DIAGNOSIS: scene inspection is scoped to the owning connection
(DES-086) by design -- it is a security boundary and correctly refused every
attempt to read another client's tree. Diagnosing this therefore required
instrumenting vox's own installed package to log its own renders, which is the
right way round. No change to that boundary is being asked for here.

WORKAROUND: restart luxd to clear orphaned connections.

Reported from vox; vox-side bead is vox-wgru.

=====================================================================
2026-08-30 15:00 -- SCOPE CORRECTION
=====================================================================
This bead was filed as the root cause of the vox Music widget flipping between
album states (vox-wgru). THAT CLAIM IS RETRACTED: the operator restarted both
hub and display, and the flip recurred afterwards. Neither retains state across
a restart, so an orphaned connection cannot have been the cause.

What remains VALID and worth fixing on its own merits: the Hub was observed
holding two connections for identity 'voxd' at the same time --

    e888eb168472  voxd  connected=25.79h  scenes=['vox.music']
    222b70a5765a  voxd  connected= 0.18h  scenes=[]

-- while exactly one voxd process and one socket to 8430 existed, and voxd had
been restarted twice in the preceding 40 minutes. The 25.79h record survived
those restarts, kept counting, and kept ownership of vox.music. Its 30s lease
did not evict it. Whether or not it caused the widget symptom, a connection
whose transport is gone should not persist or retain scene ownership.

Two smaller observations from the same session, each possibly its own bead:
- 'lux frame close <local_id>' returns success ('closed:vox.music') for a frame
  the caller does not own and which is not removed. A no-op reported as success.
- vox logged 'luxd holds no vox.music frame to raise' at 14:15:32 while the
  display log recorded 'raise frame=e888eb168472139fvox.music applied' at the
  same second -- hub and display disagreeing about whether the frame exists.

vox-640w was linked here as a duplicate on the strength of the retracted claim;
that link should be re-examined rather than trusted.

title: Library leaks its internal REST client — encapsulate, don't expose (AppletRunner._rest, top-level rest_client.py)
description:
The Python library leaks its internal REST client. AppletRunner exposes a public accessor that hands the internal client to applet code — an encapsulation defect, not a rename hazard.

## The rule

Every Punt Labs project realizes the four-surface engine-and-clients model (punt-kit/standards/architecture.md, canonical). The **library** is one of the four thin client surfaces. Its public API is what consumers import. Its transport — the HTTP client that speaks REST to luxd — is an implementation detail. Not a class anyone imports by name. Not something the library hands out.

## The current state (leaks the internal client three ways)

1. **The REST client is public.** src/punt_lux/rest_client.py defines a top-level LuxRestClient. Removed from __init__.__all__ in 0.27 but still importable as 'from punt_lux.rest_client import LuxRestClient' — external consumers (z-spec today, anyone tomorrow) reach past LuxClient into the transport.
2. **The applet runner hands it out.** AppletRunner._rest() (applets/runner.py:84,91) returns LuxRestClient for applets to consume. A runner passing an internal transport class to an applet is the *library's own* code proving the class is public in practice, whatever __all__ says.
3. **Every applet is typed on it.** applets/applet_board.py:78, applets/service.py:51,61, applets/beads_service.py:97 — the applet base classes accept LuxRestClient as a parameter type, so any applet author writes the type name and depends on it existing.

Combined, the internal transport is (1) importable, (2) handed out, and (3) written into applet signatures — three public exposures. Removing it from __all__ closed none of them.

## The target state (encapsulation, not deletion)

- **LuxClient** — the one public library class. Every library consumer (external, applet, test) imports it and only it.
- **Internal REST transport** — a private class of LuxClient. Renamed to _RestTransport (or similar), moved under a private module path (e.g. src/punt_lux/_client/_rest_transport.py). Not in any __init__.py. Not importable by name from outside the LuxClient implementation.
- **AppletRunner has NO client accessor.** No _rest(), no _client(), nothing. An applet that needs a library client constructs LuxClient.for_identity(self.identity) itself, exactly like z-spec or any external caller.
- **Applet base classes drop the client parameter.** acknowledge()/service()/work() do not receive a client. If an applet needs one, it holds LuxClient as a self.-attribute it constructed in its own __new__.
- **rest_transport.py** (HttpTransport, HubUnavailableError) stays as-is — that IS the transport layer LuxClient composes internally. Legitimate primitive. Not part of this scope.

## Not scope

- rest_transport.py / HttpTransport / HubUnavailableError — legitimate HTTP transport primitives
- LuxHubClient (WS listener) — separate surface, not this leak
- Vocabulary parity work (lux-0shg epic) — related, sibling concern

## Relation to lux-0shg

Epic lux-0shg (client surface parity) governs *what* the four surfaces expose and *how* their vocabularies align. This bead governs *what the library keeps private*. Related but separable: fixing the encapsulation leak does not require the vocabulary rename train to land, and the vocabulary train does not by itself close the leak.

## Design questions the design mission must answer

1. Applet-to-client relationship: does the applet construct LuxClient.for_identity() in its __new__ once and hold it? Does the applet base class own that so every applet gets self.client for free? Does AppletRunner set an environment or context the applet reads from?
2. Sync-vs-async: LuxClient is async (per 0.27). Applets today are sync. Options: (a) applets become async; (b) LuxClient adds sync passthroughs; (c) applet base class exposes .run(coro) that .run_until_complete()'s under the hood. Design picks one with reasoning.
3. Private-module layout: where does the encapsulated transport live? src/punt_lux/_client/? src/punt_lux/_internal/rest_transport.py? Leading-underscore module vs leading-underscore package vs a top-level _client package?
4. rest_client_scenes.py + rest_client_display.py (the concern-split modules composed by the current LuxRestClient): does LuxClient already have equivalent noun-grouped accessors (per lux-0shg vocabulary), or are these families absorbed into LuxClient? Verify against current LuxClient shape.
5. Post-migration verification: 'grep -rn LuxRestClient src/ tests/ docs/' returns zero. 'from punt_lux.rest_client import' returns zero. Any surviving public module in src/punt_lux/ containing REST/HTTP-transport class definitions returns zero.

## Discovery

Vox agent working on z-spec migration (z-spec-t7w) flagged that z-spec still imports LuxRestClient. Investigation showed the class is still active internally as the applet transport — retirement was cosmetic, not real. Operator's framing: 'We have an actual REST API, there is no need to have a Python client that hands out a REST client in Python.'

title: ADR needed: applet identity pid convention (SESSION vs OWN) — lux and z-spec differ, no guidance for future authors
description:
# Applet identity pid convention — SESSION pid (lux) vs OWN pid (z-spec)

Two live applet identity implementations use different pid tokens, both defensible on their own terms, with no ADR pointing a future applet author at which to copy.

## The two conventions in the wild

**lux (`AppletIdentity.for_session`)** — carries the **SESSION** pid.

`src/punt_lux/applets/identity.py`. The rationale (from the class docstring, added in punt-lux 0.24.0): "the entry belongs to the session. An applet restarted against a live session comes back as the same identity and takes its own entry over, which is what the succession rules are for."

**z-spec (`ZSpecLuxIdentity`)** — carries its **OWN** process pid.

`punt_zspec/lux/identity.py:54-55`, `name=f"{_TOOL_NAME} #{os.getpid()}"`. The rationale (from z-spec's own comment): a declared pid naming another process "would be a token that lies."

## Both are defensible

lux's model treats the menu entry as belonging to the *session*: an applet crash-restart against a live session takes the same identity back and reclaims its entry, so the session doesn't lose its menu item to an applet crash.

z-spec's model treats the pid in the name as a truth claim about the declaring process: if the process id in the name is the SESSION's, the string "lies" — it names a process that isn't the one holding the connection.

They resolve different lifetimes: lux wants entry lifetime bound to the session; z-spec wants entry lifetime bound to the tool process.

## The problem

There's no ADR — anywhere in lux, z-spec, or punt-kit — that flags the tension or points a new applet author at the right convention for their case. A future applet author reading both for guidance will find two conventions and no note saying which to copy.

Both conventions independently arrived at the same OUTER insight (program token in the distinctness string prevents applet collisions in one session), which is a good design-convergence signal — that piece is settled. The pid nuance is the unresolved dimension.

## Recommended follow-up (this bead)

Write a short ADR in lux DESIGN.md that:

1. Names both conventions.
2. States the lifetime question the choice answers: "does this applet's menu entry belong to the session (survives applet crash-restart) or to the applet process (goes away when the process does)?"
3. Gives a decision rule for future authors: session-bound applet with per-session state → SESSION pid; independent tool that happens to also render a menu entry → OWN pid.
4. Notes that current `AppletIdentity.for_session` encodes the SESSION-pid choice, and that a tool preferring OWN-pid semantics should build its own identity type rather than reuse `AppletIdentity` (as z-spec does).

Not urgent — no applet author is being confused right now. Filed so it doesn't get lost.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the vox agent (claude:tty29) during the lux-e6i4 cross-repo coordination on 2026-08-14, while surveying which repos consume `AppletIdentity.for_session`. z-spec doesn't, because it built its own — and reading z-spec's rationale exposed the tension.
notes: 2026-08-15 (post-merge coordination with vox agent claude:tty29): promoting from documentation note to genuine design bead. Vox agent's framing (correct): 'Whichever way it lands, it should land explicitly rather than by whichever value happened to be in scope at the call site.' Current state — code that carries whichever pid was in scope when it was written — is the slow-time-domain variant of the 'green while wrong' failure class. Needs a design mission that picks one convention with a stated rationale (SESSION-pid because entry belongs to session; OWN-pid because a declared pid naming another process 'would be a token that lies') and applies it uniformly, then codifies which is which for future applet authors.

title: Agent menu_set items are dead on click — no frame_id binding, no click routing to owner
description:
Live smoke test 0.32.1 (2026-09-11): clicking an agent-registered menu item (via MCP menu_set) does nothing. Applet items (lux-beads 'Beads') work. Confirmed the click IS captured (event_ls shows agent item ids with action=menu) but is actioned nowhere. Root cause is TWO independent gaps (code trace, read-only):

(a) menu_set items structurally cannot carry a frame_id. domain/hub/menu_models.py Menu._entry_from_wire (lines ~111-139) builds MenuAction from only {id,label,shortcut,icon} and never reads frame_id from the agent's dict — even though MenuAction.frame_id exists (menu_models.py:39), to_wire serializes it, and the display WireAction.of_payload (display/menus/wire.py:113) would honor it. So an agent item is ALWAYS frame_id=None, and the display's frame-raise branch (display/menus/wire_decode.py:86-87) never fires for it. The tool docstring (tools/display_write_tools.py:30-31) documents only {label,id}.

(b) A frameless menu click reaches the Hub but is dropped. wire_decode.py:_invoke.activate (85-96) ALWAYS emits a RemoteEventHandlerInvocation(action='menu', element_id=<item id>) back to the Hub. display_link _dispatch (domain/hub/display_link.py:288-315) falls through to HubInteractionDispatch.dispatch (hub_interaction_dispatch.py:40-49), which for action=='menu' calls _dispatch_menu_callback(element_id) (91-119). That requires CallbackInvocation.from_menu_id (domain/hub/session_callback.py:89-100) — id must be 'connection_id<US>callback_id'. An agent item id (e.g. 'agent_smoke') has no unit separator → ValueError → 'menu click for a non-callback leaf id; ignoring' → dropped. There is NO path delivering an agent-menu click to the registering session's inbox. topic_recv is publish-only (subscribe_tools.py:88-96); callback_pending only peeks a count (99-109).

Applets sidestep BOTH: they register a CALLBACK (applets/leg.py:135-139 register_callback with frame_id) — routable leaf id (covers b) that also carries frame_id (covers a). Agents have neither on the menu_set surface.

Fix dimensions: (a) let menu_set items carry frame_id → display-local raise (closes the operator's exact 'close frame, reopen from menu' case, matches applets, minimal MCP-surface change); (b) route agent-menu clicks by owning session into a drainable inbox so a listening agent can handle arbitrary clicks (larger; needs new recv plumbing). Operator ruling needed on scope (a only / a+b) before implementation — this is an MCP tool-surface/protocol change.
