title: Hub silently accepts second callback set on a connection from a different program (defense-in-depth for lux-e6i4)
description:
# Hub silently accepts second callback registration on a connection from a different program

The lux-e6i4 fix (0.24.0) makes `AppletIdentity` scope by declaring program, so two applets in one session can no longer derive the same connection through the intended path. But the underlying Hub behaviour that produced the silent failure is unchanged: **the Hub silently accepts a second `register_callback` set on an existing connection**, even when the callbacks come from a different program than the one already registered there. The first program's callbacks are clobbered, no error is raised, no log line records the event, no field in `list_clients` reflects it.

That's the exact failure this morning's incident manifested as. From the live Hub state before the fix propagated to Jim's machine:

- Connection `d942f4eccedbbc7b` (identity `"lux · lux · #12893"`) owned scene `beads-lux` but was subscribed only to `vox.*` topics.
- The `lux` submenu rendered BOTH a `Beads` entry AND a `Vox` entry, each pointing at that one connection.
- Clicking `Beads` dispatched to a handler that no longer existed.

The pre-fix symptom was NOT a missing menu entry. It was two correct-looking entries, one of which was a dead control. No error, no log line, no visual tell. A user discovers it by clicking and getting nothing.

## Why the current fix is not enough on its own

The lux-e6i4 fix eliminates the ONE known way this could happen (two applets in the same session deriving the same identity). It does NOT prevent:

1. A third applet arriving later with a `_PROGRAM` token that happens to collide with an existing one (namespace clash across the applet ecosystem).
2. A caller constructing a `ClientIdentity` by hand with a colliding `name` field.
3. Future refactoring that adds a new derivation path we haven't foreseen.

In each case the silent-clobber behaviour returns unchanged.

## Suggested defensive moves (pick one, cheap)

The Hub already sees enough state to detect the collision: at `register_callback` time it knows the connection and any callbacks already on it. Options:

1. **Reject** — `register_callback` fails with a specific error naming both programs (the incumbent and the arriving one). The arriving applet sees the failure and can log/exit. Strongest guarantee; may surprise applet authors.
2. **Log loudly** — the Hub emits a warning-level log entry naming both programs and the connection. Cheapest to implement. Downside: only surfaces to log-readers, not to the applet.
3. **Surface in `list_clients`** — add a `callback_conflicts: []` field per client, listing programs whose registrations were superseded. Diagnosable via introspection; no runtime behaviour change. Useful for anyone doing what the vox agent did this morning.

Combinations are fine — reject at the boundary AND surface the conflict in `list_clients` for the ones that got through in older code.

## Not urgent

lux-e6i4 is closed and shipped. The specific bug is fixed by identity distinctness. This bead is defense-in-depth for the failure class the fix belongs to — worth doing when the applet epic (`lux-mxvy`) is being implemented and the Hub's callback registration path is being touched anyway.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the vox agent (claude:tty29) on 2026-08-14 during closing local review on the vox-iyny mirror PR. Their framing: "identity distinctness is sufficient for the bug, but defence in depth is worth a deliberate decision — file it or dismiss it, but see the question."
notes:
2026-08-14 (silent-failure-hunter finding on lux-k3u6): related dispatch-side gap — when a menu click arrives at the Hub carrying a connection_id the registry no longer knows (e.g., senior applet departed between menu composition and Display re-push, click on cached Details menu), the click silently drops. Should log at WARNING and either return a diagnostic to the caller or surface in list_errors. Same 'silent failure' class this bead is scoped to detect at REGISTRATION time; this is the DISPATCH-time twin. When implementing lux-tfn1, extend to cover both phases.
2026-08-15 (post-merge coordination with vox agent claude:tty29): promoting from note to actively-filed P2. Vox agent's night surfaced the same failure class in four different vox incidents (exception class with zero raise sites, coupling baseline sentinels, ratchet silently not scoring new files, 72 audio playbacks logging irrelevant env vars). All 'signal reports success while not doing the thing.' The dispatch-side dead-connection-id gap is the same class here: a click for a stale connection_id drops silently. Scope INCLUDES the dispatch-side detection (log at WARNING, surface in list_errors, or reject at dispatch) alongside the registration-side detection this bead was originally scoped to. Do not defer; this is the class of bug that survives specifically because it has no symptom.

title: Lease-reap departure incomplete vs graceful disconnect (leaks subs/writer/inbox)
description: Timer-reap (LeaseReapSweep -> reap_lapsed_leases -> _depart_lapsed) frees registry+ownership only. It never runs hub.on_disconnect (drops subscriptions + writer binding) nor the transport on_disconnect sink (releases the MCP inbox queue) that lifecycle.disconnect_connection runs on graceful disconnect. So a timer-reaped connection leaks its subscriptions, writer binding, and inbox queue, and retains dead deliveries, even though it no longer appears in clients.sessions(). Fix: converge the timer-reap onto the full departure cascade. Needs design (domain-layer sweep must reach per-session transport on_disconnect sinks) + model extension (connection_lease_reaping.tex Depart should cover the full cascade, not just registry+ownership) + run-and-prove that subs/writer/inbox are freed. Found by Copilot on PR #459 (lux-d84d).
close_reason: Implemented + merged via PR: lease-reap departure now runs the full four-step cascade (registry+ownership+subscriptions/writer+inbox) on every trigger via a DepartureSinks coordinator, and register_client/identify_client are under StoreLock so a same-identity reconnect can't be corrupted by a stale reap's cascade tail. Verified: ProB round-3 model (I1-I7 + deadlock, setsize 2 exhaustive; 2 fidelity controls), a fidelity-tested reconnect-race test (fails without the lock, passes with), run-and-prove via the lux-221j introspection (one sweep frees registry/ownership/subs/writer/inbox together), 3 review agents sound.

title: EPIC: kit-manager — settle where per-repo config lives, then build on it
description:
Batch: everything that changes where per-repo config lives and what punt does to a
repo it is pointed at.

WHY THESE BELONG TOGETHER
qv4 decides WHERE a repo declares what it uses. pjwn builds the command that
writes that declaration. mb8k reads it to scope audit. s00b rolls the result
across the fleet. Build any of them before qv4 settles and the others encode a
location that then moves.

This is the one batch where the ordering is not a convenience — it is a hard
dependency. A rollout (s00b) that deploys the wrong config location has to be
redone in ~25 repos.

MEMBERS
  pkit-qv4   P2  Filesystem standard: per-repo config in .punt-labs/<tool>/,
                 not repo-root sentinels. THIS IS THE BLOCKER — it defines the
                 location everything else writes to and reads from.
  pkit-pjwn  P1  Kit-manager surface: punt enable (self) + punt install/enable
                 <tool> dispatch, absorbing the init section 2.1 fix.
  pkit-mb8k  P2  Scope punt audit to a repo's declared kit. Also listed under the
                 audit epic — it is genuinely in both, because it reads the
                 declaration (this epic) and changes findings (that one).
  pkit-s00b  P2  Rollout: strip org duplicates + punt auto claude across all
                 repos.

NOTE ON pjwn's PRIORITY. It is P1 and qv4 is P2, but qv4 blocks it. Either qv4
rises to P1 or pjwn waits — worth the operator deciding rather than letting the
priorities imply an order the dependency forbids.

EVIDENCE THAT THE LOCATION QUESTION IS LIVE. As of 2026-08-14 punt-kit's own tree
carries per-tool config in BOTH shapes: .punt-labs/vox/, .punt-labs/quarry/,
.punt-labs/ethos/ alongside root-level .biff, .vox, .lux. The canonical .gitignore
rollout now has explicit rules for both. So the standard is not describing a
convention that exists; it is choosing between two that both exist. That makes it
a decision bead, not a documentation bead, and it should be treated as one.

CROSS-EPIC MEMBER. mb8k appears here and in the audit epic. That is deliberate,
not a filing error — it is the seam between the two, and whichever epic starts
first should expect to negotiate with the other over it.

title: EPIC: audit engine — a findings type, then the consumers that need it
description:
Batch: everything that changes what `punt audit` produces or who can consume it.

WHY THESE BELONG TOGETHER
Three of these add a CONSUMER of audit findings and two change what findings
exist. Every consumer needs the same thing first: a stable findings
representation. Today audit returns list[tuple[str, str, str]] — a status glyph,
a label, and a message string — assembled for terminal printing. Nothing else can
consume that without parsing rendered output.

Build the MCP surface and the REST surface separately and each one invents its own
serialisation of the same tuples, and the judgment examiner has nowhere structured
to put a verdict. Do the findings type once and all three become thin.

MEMBERS
  pkit-zmca  P1  Standards auditor agent: punt audit gains a judgment examiner,
                 one standard per run. Produces findings that are not
                 pass/fail-per-rule, which is exactly what the current tuple
                 cannot express.
  pkit-mb8k  P2  Scope punt audit to a repo's declared kit. Changes which checks
                 run, so it changes what a consumer sees.
  pkit-1up8  P3  MCP server exposing audit, status, and playbook launch.
  pkit-mud6  P3  REST surface for findings and run status, for CI and dashboards.
  pkit-jsxe  P4  Add a punt audit check for tracked bd runtime artifacts.

ORDERING IS FORCED, not preferred:
  1. A findings type that carries severity, rule identity, location and remedy.
     Not a new bead — it is the first task inside zmca, because zmca is the
     member that cannot be built without it.
  2. mb8k, which decides which checks contribute findings.
  3. 1up8 and mud6 in parallel, both thin adapters at that point.
  jsxe rides along whenever convenient; it is one more check, not a design change.

STATUS CORRECTION ON jsxe, verified 2026-08-14: the fleet-wide sweep is NOT
complete — mcp-proxy still tracks .beads/daemon-error. The bead title says
'swept fleet-wide'. One repo remains, and the preventive audit check does not
exist at all, which is the part that matters.

WHAT THIS EPIC IS NOT. It is not a mandate to build MCP and REST surfaces. Both
are P3 and may never be worth it. The point of batching is that IF they are built,
they must not each define their own findings format. If the operator decides
neither surface is wanted, zmca and mb8k still need the findings type and this
epic still holds.

title: Standards auditor agent: punt audit gains a judgment examiner, one standard per run
description: Agreed design (operator rulings 2026-08-02, discussed one question at a time). THE FEATURE: one auditor agent whose reference is the named standard — 'punt audit --standard readme' style invocation, run on ONE standard at a time at the user's direction (hard constraint: never the whole corpus in one run — context explodes; coverage comes from many small engagements over time). (4) One shared enforcement harness prompt + standard-as-reference; no per-standard hand-authored agents (a new standard is auditable the day it is written). title: Add standalone CLI
description:

Minimum CLI surface:
- prfaq init — scaffold a project with research/ directory and prfaq.tex template

- prfaq doctor — verify LaTeX dependencies (see related bead)

The generation, review, meeting, and feedback workflows are inherently AI-driven and belong in the plugin. But compilation, scaffolding, and health checks are deterministic and should work without Claude.

title: Auto-ingest ./research/ into quarry database when quarry is available
description:
## Problem

The researcher agent checks for quarry's search_documents tool and uses it if available, but nothing in the plugin creates a quarry database or ingests the ./research/ directory. Users who have quarry installed get no benefit unless they manually set up a database and ingest their files outside the plugin.

## Proposed Behavior

During Phase 0 (research discovery), if quarry MCP tools are available:

1. Check if a project-scoped quarry database exists (e.g., database name derived from project directory or prfaq.tex title)
2. If not, create one via use_database
3. Register ./research/ directory via register_directory (quarry watches for changes) or ingest files via ingest_auto
4. Researcher agent then uses search_documents against the project database for semantic search over all research files

This makes quarry integration zero-config — install quarry, drop files in ./research/, and the plugin handles the rest.

## Design Questions

- Database naming: per-project (directory name) or per-document (prfaq title)?
- Should the plugin register_directory (persistent, auto-syncs) or ingest_auto (one-shot)? register_directory is better for iterative workflows where research files accumulate across sessions.
- Should this happen in Phase 0 of /prfaq, in the researcher agent, or in a SessionStart hook?
- What about users who already have a quarry database with relevant content? Don't want to fragment their search across two databases.

title: Connector onboarding UX so the researcher agent can use internal data sources
description:
## Problem

PR/FAQ research is limited to the ./research/ folder plus internet search. Operators have internal data sources — Databricks, Jira, Confluence, Linear, Google Analytics, CRM, data warehouses — reachable via MCP servers or other means. That is where the real customer evidence lives: actual support tickets, actual usage data, actual roadmap history. The tool ignores all of it.

## Defect discovered while scoping (fix as part of this work)

plugin/agents/researcher.md lines 50-58 instruct the agent to check for and use quarry-mcp, financial data servers, statistical databases, product analytics, and CRM data. Its frontmatter tools: line grants ONLY 'Read, Write, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch' — no MCP tools whatsoever. The agent is told to use tools it cannot see.

Line 58 compounds it: 'If a tool is not available, skip it silently — do not error.' So every internal source is skipped, silently, on every run. The operator receives a research report that appears complete with no signal that internal sources were never consulted. This is a silent failure of exactly the class org standards ban.

The agent description (line 5) also advertises 'optional MCP data providers' — a capability the frontmatter cannot deliver. False advertising in the agent contract.

plugin/agents/peer-reviewer.md line 70 has the identical gap: it instructs quarry-mcp use with no MCP tools granted.

## Proposed change

1. Grant the researcher agent access to MCP tools so the instructions in its own prompt body are executable.

2. Replace silent-skip with explicit reporting. When a declared source is unreachable or a claim has no internal evidence, the research output must SAY SO. An operator must always be able to tell which sources were consulted and which were not.

3. Build a connector onboarding UX. The operator declares their internal sources once — what exists, what each is authoritative for, how to query it — and the declaration persists for future runs. Probing for tool names is not onboarding.

4. Wire the declared connectors into the research process so internal sources are consulted BEFORE the open internet. Internal primary data outranks a web search, the same way ./research/ primary data already does.

## Design questions to resolve before implementation

- Where does the connector declaration live? A file under ./research/, a project-level config, or a section in the .tex itself?
- Is onboarding a distinct command (/prfaq:connect) or a step inside the existing Phase 0 research discovery?
- How are connectors described so the researcher can query them without hardcoding per-vendor logic? (capability + example query per source, vs. a fixed vendor registry)
- Citation format for internal sources — a Jira ticket or a Databricks query result is not a biblatex web citation. What does an internal-source citation look like in the .bib?
- Trust and provenance: internal data is unpublished. How is it distinguished from published evidence in the document so a reader knows which claims rest on private data?

## Why it matters

Same root cause as prfaq-bxn: authors cannot envision real customer questions and concerns. The company's own support tickets, analytics, and roadmap history are the highest-quality answer to that problem, and the tool currently cannot reach any of it.
notes:
## Operator clarification (2026-09-09): PR/FAQs are INTERNAL documents

The PR/FAQ is read by people inside the company. There is no external reader. This settles the residual citation question:

- No external-verifiability problem exists. A reader can open the Jira ticket, rerun the Databricks query, and load the dashboard.
- The internal-source citation needs only to support REPRODUCIBILITY — enough identifying detail to find the source again (ticket ID, query text, dataset name, extraction date). Exactly the job a URL performs for a web source. Nothing more.
- No disclaimer, hedge, or provenance caveat of any kind. There is no audience to disclaim to.

Note on framing: the document is shaped like a press release but is a DECISION document. Do not design for external publication.

Naming check against prfaq-bxn: 'External FAQs' in that bead means external STAKEHOLDER GROUPS (customers, partners, regulators), not an externally published artifact. The two uses of 'external' do not conflict — but the reference guides should not imply the document itself is published.

title: Installer writes global permission rules; Write() rules now warn at every session start
description: install.sh injects 22 permission rules into the user's global ~/.claude/settings.json. Eight are Write(path) rules, which Claude Code no longer matches — it prints a warning per rule at every session start, in every project, for every installed user. Root cause: (1) permissions must never be written to the global settings file; (2) path-scoped rules must use Edit(path), which covers Write/Edit/NotebookEdit. Fix end to end: stop writing global rules, clean up rules previously injected, move to project-scoped opt-in, correct docs, release.

title: Lux integration: meeting decision dashboard
description:
Lux integration: meeting decision dashboard for PR/FAQ review.

Architecture: Option D hybrid — prfaq-specific skill prompt + Lux dashboard template.

The prfaq plugin creates a skill (auto-activated during /prfaq:meeting or /prfaq:meeting-hive) that composes Lux elements into a decision dashboard:

1. Hot-spot map — tree element showing document structure (press release → sections, FAQs by category, risk assessment). Color-coded by risk: red=critical issues identified by personas, yellow=ambiguous/needs iteration, green=approved. Updated as personas debate.

2. Persona cards — four group elements in columns layout, one per persona (Priya/customer, Dana/builder, Wei/engineer, Alex/executive). Each shows: verdict badge (APPROVE/ITERATE/REJECT), key quote, biggest concern. Updated in real-time during /prfaq:meeting-hive as personas reach consensus.

3. Risk matrix — draw canvas with 2x2 grid (likelihood × impact), risk items as labeled dots positioned in quadrants. Visual summary of the four-risks assessment.

4. Version diff — two markdown panels side-by-side showing before/after text when /prfaq:feedback redrafts sections. Adapts the data-explorer split-view pattern.

5. Meeting playback — during /prfaq:meeting-listen, show speaker cards updating in sequence with Vox narrating each persona's position. Visual debate timeline.

Delivery mechanism:
- Skill prompt in prfaq plugin encodes dashboard layout as JSON templates
- Reuses Lux dashboard and status-board patterns
- Integrates with existing /prfaq:meeting workflow — Lux shows what the conversation describes
- MCP instructions provide formatting rules via Prior-Context Priming

title: test-wheel.sh aborts its own search round-trip on a head -N line-count bug
description: scripts/test-wheel.sh fails at the search round-trip step with 'head: illegal line count -- -1' — a computed head -N argument goes negative, so make test-wheel exits 1 even though build/install/import/providers/CLI/doctor/serve all PASS. The wheel + daemon are fine; the script's own verification step is broken. Fix the line-count computation (guard against N<1) so the search round-trip actually runs. Found during quarry-3a7f wheel verification.

title: Robust fire-and-forget: opt-in poll of a dispatched task result plus real CLI exit codes
description: Task-dispatching CLI commands are fire-and-forget by operator ruling 2026-07-17: the client dispatches, the daemon does light acceptance-validation and returns 2xx accepted or 4xx rejected, and the client returns on acceptance without waiting for async processing. Intentional — a large ingest crawl or sync runs for minutes daemon-side and must not block the client. Accepted consequence: a command can exit 0 on acceptance while the daemon operation later fails, e.g. disable with keep-data false returns before the purge completes so failed chunks stay searchable. This feature adds an opt-in wait: a follow flag or a quarry wait command that polls the daemon task_status for the terminal result and maps it to a real exit code and rendered output, WITHOUT making the default path block. QuarryClient already has await_task and TaskOutcome and the daemon exposes task_status. Operator: a more robust fire and forget and return code style logic would poll the daemon for the result, a larger design effort.

title: DES-031 PR 4: mcp_server.py stdio path — collapse to thin proxy or drop
description:
Implements DES-031. The stdio MCP path in mcp_server.py is a full engine instance: loads ONNX, opens LanceDB, runs the pipeline. mcp-proxy (the Go binary) already provides stdio-to-daemon bridging — the Python stdio MCP server is duplicate machinery.

Two options to evaluate during the design mission:
1. Drop mcp_server.py stdio mode entirely. All MCP clients use mcp-proxy → daemon WebSocket. The /mcp WebSocket endpoint on the daemon stays.
2. Keep mcp_server.py but as a thin proxy that translates stdio MCP calls to HTTPS or WebSocket calls to the daemon.

Option 1 is simpler; option 2 preserves a fallback if mcp-proxy is unavailable. Recommendation comes out of the design mission.

Scope:
- Decide option 1 vs option 2 with the specialist.
- If option 1: remove mcp_server.py stdio surface; update plugin.json, README, CLAUDE.md references.
- If option 2: gut mcp_server.py down to ~100 lines of MCP-to-HTTPS proxying. No engine imports.
- The /mcp WebSocket endpoint in http_server.py stays — that is the daemon's MCP surface and is correct.

Delegation: rmh (worker), mdm (evaluator).

Acceptance:
- mcp_server.py contains no engine imports.
- Existing MCP tool tests pass (re-routed to the daemon).
- Plugin still works end-to-end after install: Claude Code → mcp-proxy → daemon → response.

Depends on: PR 2 (HTTP API completeness).

title: transcript_reader minor hardening: budget separator accounting + non-string role guard
description: Deferred from PR #370 (immaterial, djb-confirmed behavior-preserving). Two Copilot nits on the new TranscriptReader: (1) _join_within_budget sums part lengths but inserts '\n\n' separators, so the joined string can exceed _MAX_CHARS by ~2*(parts-1) chars — immaterial on a 500K front-truncation budget, but account for the separators for exactness. (2) message_text uses the untrusted 'role' field without isinstance(str) validation — existing behavior carried over from extract_message_text (djb: behavior-preserving, no regression), on untrusted transcript content; add a defensive isinstance guard. Both low-risk polish on newly-extracted code.

title: Single-command setup with editor detection
description: Consideration: Context7's 'npx ctx7 setup' detects the user's editor and configures everything in one command. Quarry's install.sh already does this but is heavier (downloads model, sets up daemon, configures MCP, etc.). Consider whether a lighter 'quarry setup' path could exist for users who already have quarry installed and just need MCP/editor configuration — especially relevant for remote server setup (quarry-m266).

title: remember has no durable copy — drain-abort under deep backlog silently loses an admitted remember
description: djb concurrency review of DES-042 (quarry-lxrk): captures survive a drain-timeout-abort because the transcript .md/archive predates the POST, but remember has NO durable client-side artifact and 'quarry remember' is fire-and-forget (cli_ingest.py:145 does not await_task; mcp_server.py:225 same if the agent doesn't poll). So a remember admitted (202 returned, caller gone) then aborted by a drain timeout under a backlog deeper than ingest_drain_timeout_s (at embed gate=1) is lost with no durable copy and no caller notification. Narrow (requires shutdown while backlog > drain timeout) and intersects a pre-existing property (remember was always no-durable-copy + fire-and-forget, so a crash mid-ingest could always lose it) — the queue adds a new but comparable loss window. The design's §3.4 durability argument covers captures only. Fix options: (a) give remember a durable client-side spool (like captures' .md) so backfill can recover it; (b) on drain, run admitted remembers to completion preferentially / extend the remember drain budget; (c) at minimum make the abort log the lost remember truthfully instead of silent. Deferred from the DES-042 PR.

title: Carry connection-lost fail-fast behavior + test into QuarryClient (RemoteClient deleted by veb0)
description: Type-design + code review of the deregister-parity PR (commit 6d429ec) flagged that src/quarry/remote_client.py mixes two responsibilities: RemoteClient.request/get are pure transport (raise RemoteError), but find/await_task/_poll_once call typer.Exit and print via a rich Console. This drags typer/rich presentation imports into what should be a transport module (PY-IC-8 dependency-direction) and makes find internally inconsistent (happy path returns (json,text) for the caller to emit; error path exits directly). Separately, RemoteClient.find and _search_params carry 8 positional params (PY-OO-3 prefers <=4) — a faithful extraction of the old 9-arg _find_remote, but worth bundling. NOT a defect: the client works correctly and all surfaces are green. Deferred from the deregister PR because (a) it is a layering refactor, not a bug, and (b) moving exit/print logic back into __main__.py risks regressing the module_size ratchet that PR resolved via the remote_client extraction — it needs its own careful pass.
notes:
INCLUDES the poller connection-lost diagnosability fix (was item 2 of the deregister review round). Implemented + fully tested but ratchet-blocked in isolation: adding ~10 lines to remote_client.py regresses module_size 262->275, and extracting the poll methods regresses avg_params (find/_search_params carry 8 params each). This bead's refactor (bundle find's params into a query value object + move exit/print to the command layer) frees BOTH the module_size and avg_params headroom, giving the connection-lost logic a clean home. Work preserved at .tmp/deregister-parity/item2-connection-lost.patch and git stash@{0}. Behavior: cap consecutive RemoteError(status=0) reads in await_task; after 3, surface a distinct 'Cannot reach remote quarry server' error and exit 1 immediately instead of polling 'running' for 120s then printing the misleading 'registration was removed but cleanup may still be running' message. Includes item 4a (PY-TS-14 comment on _config) and item 3e (test_consecutive_unreachable_exits_before_timeout).
Rescoped: veb0 (DES-031 v2 PR3) deletes RemoteClient entirely, so the PY-IC-8 layering concern (RemoteClient mixing transport with typer.Exit/rich print) is resolved by that deletion — do NOT refactor a class being removed. What survives and MUST be carried into the new QuarryClient: (1) the connection-lost fail-fast behavior — cap consecutive RemoteError(status=0) reads in await_task; after 3, surface a distinct 'Cannot reach remote quarry server' error and exit 1 immediately, instead of polling 'running' for 120s then printing the misleading 'registration was removed but cleanup may still be running'; (2) test_consecutive_unreachable_exits_before_timeout; (3) find's query args bundled into a frozen(slots) value object (PY-OO-3, <=4 params). Preserved work: .tmp/deregister-parity/item2-connection-lost.patch and git stash@{0}. The layering + params design guidance is folded into veb0's design mission (see veb0 note).

title: Converge hooks onto QuarryClient: add content-ingest to the single daemon path + delete BackgroundIngest engine path
description: The capture/PreCompact hook is the fourth client surface and the only one still a FAT CLIENT: _hook_entry.py BackgroundIngest builds its own Database, does its own dedup, calls ingest_content, and writes LanceDB directly (lines 27/143/181) - a second divergent copy of the daemon ingest logic living in a client (bug-class-3), and the root cause of the load-77-97 capture-starvation (quarry-lnog). The design (DES-031 I1) requires all four surfaces - CLI, MCP, library, hooks - to resolve to ONE codepath: build request, hand to QuarryClient, which talks to the one daemon. PR-6 import-linter boundary CANNOT pass while the hook imports the engine. BLOCKER discovered: the shipped IngestRequest is URL-ONLY ('File upload is not part of this contract'); QuarryClient only has ingest_url; there is NO content-ingest path on the wire. The capture hook must ingest a ~500KB transcript TEXT blob - content, not a URL - so the one operation it needs is not in the contract. This traces to the earlier remove-direct-ingest scope call (URL + register/sync only). title: SessionStart marker gate + reconcile drift; quarry disable must deregister
description:
`handle_session_start` (`src/quarry/hooks.py:201-296`) auto-registers any
cwd whose parent isn't already covered, without consulting the enabled
marker. It reads `HookConfig.session_sync` from
`.punt-labs/quarry/config.md` — a per-repo config knob — but never
imports `EnabledMarker`. Result: nine of ten registered collections are
indexed-but-mute, because `quarry enable` is the operation that (per
`punt-kit/standards/tool-enable-disable.md` § 2.3):

1. deposits `<repo>/.punt-labs/quarry/CLAUDE.md` (the vendored guide);
2. writes the `<repo>/.punt-labs/quarry/enabled` marker;
3. adds `@.punt-labs/quarry/CLAUDE.md` to `<repo>/CLAUDE.md`;
4. registers the collection.

Auto-registration bypasses (1)–(3), so the marker is the only signal
that separates "the user opted in and got the guide" from "quarry ran a
walk-up match on my cwd and indexed me silently."

Diagnosis: `docs/investigations/2026-08-30-agent-integration-gap.md`,
root cause 2; intervention 5. Design decision ruled 2026-08-30: the
marker is authoritative. SessionStart consults it and takes one of three
paths.

## Scope

Add an `EnabledMarker(cwd).exists()` check at the top of
`handle_session_start` in `src/quarry/hooks.py` (after `cwd` and
`config` resolution, before covering-collection lookup). Branch on the
combination of *marker present?* and *registration exists?*.

### Path A: marker present, registration exists (or auto-registrable)

Current behavior. Walk-up covering match; if none, auto-register; kick
off background sync; return the (rewritten by `lqup`)
`additionalContext`.

### Path B: marker absent, no registration exists

**Refuse to auto-register.** Return an `additionalContext` telling the
agent quarry is available for this repo but not enabled, and pointing at
`quarry enable <cwd>` as the on-ramp per
`tool-enable-disable.md` § 2.3. Do not touch the registry, do not write
chunks, do not deposit the guide.

### Path C: marker absent, registration exists (the reconciliation case)

The state the user's question surfaced: someone deleted the marker (or
never had one — the pre-existing mute repos) but the collection stays in
the registry. Auto-behavior here is destructive: deregistering wipes
chunks per the keep-data policy, and doing that silently on SessionStart
would delete a user's data based on marker drift.

**Refuse to auto-deregister. Refuse to auto-register.** Return an
`additionalContext` that:

- Names the inconsistency in one line.
- Offers two paths: `quarry enable <cwd>` (re-adopt, restore the marker
  and guide) or `quarry deregister <cwd>` (drop the registration and its
  chunks).
- Logs a warning for observability.

This is not the same as the retroactive cleanup pass — that is
`quarry disable` doing its job (marker gone ⇒ deregister the collection,
per § 2.9 dormant rules). SessionStart's job is to surface the drift and
name the two doors, not to walk through them.

### Ancillary

Update the daemon-unreachable branch (`hooks.py:279-290`): if the marker
is present but the daemon is down, keep the existing defer message; if
the marker is absent, the daemon-state check is moot — return the "not
enabled here" message in either branch.

## Also required (in this bead)

**Add `deregister` to `quarry disable`.** The tool-enable-disable
standard § 2.3 disable spec removes the CLAUDE.md import, deletes the
marker, and deregisters hooks — but does not deregister the *sync
registration*, which is quarry-specific. Currently `quarry disable`
leaves the collection registered, which means a user who disables never
actually stops indexing. Fix in the same PR: `disable` deregisters the
collection (matching the vox pattern from tool-enable-disable.md § 2.9
dormant vs. active). Whether disable purges chunks or leaves them in
place under keep-data is an existing quarry policy question, not a new
one — follow the current `quarry deregister` default.

## Success criteria

- `handle_session_start` calls `EnabledMarker(cwd).exists()` before any
  registry write.
- Three unit tests, one per path:
  - Path A: marker + registration → auto-sync path taken.
  - Path B: no marker, no registration → no `register_directory` call,
    `additionalContext` names `quarry enable`.
  - Path C: no marker, registration exists → no `register_directory`
    call, no `deregister_directory` call, `additionalContext` names both
    `quarry enable` and `quarry deregister`, `logger.warning` fires.
- `quarry disable` deregisters the collection; regression test asserts
  the collection is absent from `quarry list registrations` afterward.
- Existing tests for enabled repos still pass.
- Manual demo gate (WORKFLOW Level 2): start a fresh session in each of
  (a) this enabled repo, (b) an unenabled sibling with no
  `.punt-labs/quarry/enabled` and no registration, (c) an unenabled
  sibling that *does* have a stale registration. Capture the
  `additionalContext` from each transcript; confirm registered / nudge /
  reconcile behaviors.

## Not in scope

- The `additionalContext` string rewrite for enabled repos (bead
  `lqup`). This bead only defines the *unenabled* branches' messages.
- Retroactive cleanup of the nine indexed-but-mute repos — that is what
  Path C's reconcile UI is *for*; the user runs `quarry enable` or
  `quarry deregister` on each one at their own timing. This bead does
  not include a batch-cleanup command.

## References

- `punt-kit/standards/tool-enable-disable.md` — the canonical enable /
  disable contract; § 2.3 (deposit-order), § 2.9 (dormant vs. active
  distinction), § 2.11 (marker as commit point).
- `src/quarry/hooks.py:201-296` — `handle_session_start`.
- `src/quarry/enabled_marker.py:16-50` — `EnabledMarker` API (already
  symlink-safe via `SafeRepoPath`).
- `src/quarry/enablement.py` — the `Enablement` class that writes the
  marker AND deposits the guide AND adds the `@`-import; the
  authoritative on-ramp path.
- `docs/investigations/2026-08-30-agent-integration-gap.md` — cause 2,
  intervention 5.

## Owner / pairing

Worker `rmh`, evaluator `djb` (hooks touch identity, registry, and
destructive-op boundaries; djb owns the safety review). `standard`
pipeline — three-path branching plus disable-side change needs a design
mission to write out the exact state machine before implementation.

## Cluster / priority

- cluster: agent-integration
- priority: P1 (the highest-lever new-bead fix — resolves nine of ten
  mute-repo failures; other agent-integration beads are downstream of
  this one being correct)

title: cleanup: remove residual mcp-proxy references and stop using ~/.punt-labs/mcp-proxy/ paths
description:
Since the daemon-side /mcp WebSocket route was retired (quarry CHANGELOG entry, DES-031 v2.2 direction — MCP-as-client), mcp-proxy is no longer in quarry's runtime path. The `quarry mcp` stdio server is unchanged and works; the `QuarryClient` HTTP path replaces the WebSocket route. mcp-proxy itself remains supported as a tool but has no active consumer inside punt-labs (vox retired via DES-028 → voxd; lux retired via direct HTTP → luxd; biff never integrated).

Quarry still carries residual coupling to mcp-proxy in code and on-disk paths. This bead is to sweep those out.

## Residual mcp-proxy touchpoints in quarry (as of 2026-08-29)

Code:
- `src/quarry/proxy.py` — downloads and installs the mcp-proxy binary from GitHub Releases into ~/.local/bin/.
- `src/quarry/doctor.py:339-351` — `doctor` checks whether mcp-proxy is on PATH; `install` flow step 5/8 offers to install it as an optional convenience.
- `src/quarry/remote.py` — reads and writes `~/.punt-labs/mcp-proxy/quarry.toml` (URL, headers, CA cert).
- `src/quarry/client/transport.py:7` — comment states config is "absorbed from the mcp-proxy config"; the client dials HTTP directly but reads the mcp-proxy-shaped TOML.
- `src/quarry/config.py:172` — comment: "well-known port for quarryd + mcp-proxy configs".
- `scripts/build-mcpb.sh` — grep hit, may or may not still reference the binary.
- Tests: `tests/test_proxy.py`, `tests/test_doctor.py`, `tests/test_remote.py` — pin the current behavior.

On-disk paths:
- `~/.punt-labs/mcp-proxy/quarry.toml` — quarry currently writes this via `quarry login` and reads it in the client transport. Should move to a quarry-owned location (e.g. `~/.punt-labs/quarry/remote.toml` or similar — quarry owns the schema now, so it should own the path too).
- `~/.punt-labs/mcp-proxy/quarry-ca.crt` — same rationale.

## Suggested scope

1. Move the client-transport config file to a quarry-owned path (`~/.punt-labs/quarry/…`). Update `quarry login` / `quarry logout` to write there. Keep a one-release compatibility read of the old path with a deprecation warning if you want a soft cutover.
2. Delete `src/quarry/proxy.py`, remove the doctor / install optional step for the mcp-proxy binary, and drop the `remote.py` writer for the mcp-proxy TOML file (the config-writer can be adapted to write the new quarry-owned path).
3. Update `client/transport.py` comments to describe the schema as quarry's own, not "absorbed from mcp-proxy".
4. Update tests accordingly; delete `tests/test_proxy.py`.
5. Update CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]` and any doc references.

## Context / cross-repo

- Sibling PR mcp-proxy #50 (cobra migration) and #51 (README pin fix) are landing 2026-08-29 as v0.5.0. mcp-proxy is not going away — it is on-hold-not-abandoned pending a future WebSocket consumer. This bead is not about deprecating mcp-proxy; it is about ending quarry's now-vestigial couplings to it.
- Related: `pkit-pu0a` (punt-kit) tracks the release-tool bug that leaves README install SHAs stale; unrelated to this cleanup but part of the same 2026-08-29 audit.

title: Unify quarry CLI/MCP/HTTP/library naming to the noun-verb standard
description:
CLI, MCP, HTTP, and the QuarryClient library currently use divergent names for the same operations (find/search//search, register/register_directory, list_documents/document_list, one flat MCP tool per verb vs noun-scoped tools elsewhere). Bring all four client surfaces into alignment with punt-kit/standards/cli.md, verified against the actual vox and lux implementations (not just the doc): singular noun-first CLI groups, noun_verb library methods, noun-scoped MCP tools with a subcommand dispatch param, arguments disambiguate rather than separate command names.

Design decisions made in conversation with the operator (2026-08-23):
- Nouns are singular: document, collection, registration, database, capture (not documents/collections/etc.)
- ingest + remember collapse into `document add` (type inferred from argument)
- find/show/delete become search/show/remove
- search splits into two operations: `document search` (existing find behavior, ranked documents/chunks) and `collection search` (NEW capability, ranked collections -- no existing backend support, needs its own design)
- login/logout move under the existing `remote` noun group (remote list is already grouped correctly today)
- optimize/sync live under `database`; backfill-sessions lives under `capture`
- hook dispatcher goes from plural `hooks` to singular `hook`
- MCP restructures from one flat tool per verb to one tool per noun with a subcommand param, matching vox's mic:rec/mic:music pattern -- this is a bigger change than renaming
- quarry MCP is missing an `enablement` tool entirely (enable/disable should exist on every surface per tool-enable-disable.md) -- vox has one, quarry doesn't
- Open decision: db vs database as the noun (no abbreviation precedent in vox/lux, leaning `database`)
- Open decision: whether collection search (new backend capability) rides in this epic or splits out

Full before/after tables live in this session's transcript; the design mission task below re-derives and ratifies them formally before implementation starts.

title: EPIC: vox surface consistency — split model/provider/voice out of /vox, close CLI/MCP parity gaps
description:
Umbrella for a cohesive rework of vox's user-facing surface across CLI, MCP tools, slash commands, and the Lux Control Panel. Two threads converge here:

## Thread 1: Split model/provider/voice out of /vox

The current /vox slash command dispatches four unrelated concerns (model, provider, enable, disable) via a single argument parser. This is bad UX:
- The argument hint reads "model <name> | provider <name> | enable | disable" — the user can't tell what /vox does from the picker.
- enable/disable is a fleet-wide enablement pair (tool-enable-disable.md §2.14 mandates `/<tool> enable` / `/<tool> disable` — this must stay under /vox).
- model/provider are TTS config switches, unrelated to enablement — mixing them in obscures the enablement contract.

Additionally, mic:unmute is overloaded: it synthesizes text AND doubles as the model/provider/voice switch when called without text. This makes the tool's schema misleading and forces every model/provider/voice switch through a text-synthesis code path.

## Thread 2: Close CLI/MCP/panel parity gaps

An audit against punt-kit/standards/cli.md surfaced several inconsistencies beyond the model/provider/voice split, plus existing work in vox-cnak that is the same class of issue. The Lux Control Panel adds a fourth surface — and it currently exposes only voice, not provider or model. Folding all of these under one epic keeps the surface work coherent.

## Target end-state (per-function table)

| Concern | Slash | CLI | MCP | Lux panel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable/disable | /vox enable, /vox disable | vox enable, vox disable | mic:enablement | (n/a — repo-scoped) |
| Model | /vox:model [<name>] (new) | vox model [<name>] (new) | mic:model (new) | picker (new) |
| Provider | /vox:provider [<name>] (new) | vox provider [<name>] (new) | mic:provider (new) | picker (new) |
| Voice | /vox:voice [<name>] (new) | vox voice [<name>] (extended) | mic:voice (new) | picker (existing) |
| Say text | (uses mic:unmute) | vox say | mic:unmute (text-only) | (n/a — non-interactive) |
| Toggle spoken notifications | /unmute (loses [voice] arg), /mute | vox speak y\|n | mic:speak | (n/a — see notify below) |

Retired (forward integration, no shim):
- /vox model, /vox provider subcommands → /vox:model, /vox:provider top-level commands
- /unmute [voice] argument → /vox:voice
- mic:unmute overload with model=/provider=/voice= → dedicated mic:model, mic:provider, mic:voice tools
- vox voices (separate list command) → vox voice with no arg lists
- mic:who (separate list tool) → mic:voice with no arg lists

## No-argument list behavior

Every switch command (model, provider, voice) returns/displays the available list when called with no argument:
- Slash: AskUserQuestion picker with the current selection marked
- CLI: plain-text list (or JSON list under --json)
- MCP: JSON list in the tool result
- Panel: combo/picker with the current selection marked

## Notable finding — vox-0rp9.5 (mic:notify off-mode)

Flagged during the audit and worth calling out at the epic level: the MCP mic:notify tool has an `n`/off mode the CLI removed per tool-enable-disable.md §2.3, which retired the y/n vocabulary for enablement and moved the off state onto vox disable. Not just an inconsistency — it lets a caller turn spoken notifications off through what is semantically the wrong channel, bypassing the marker-based enablement contract §2.3 mandates as the sole enable/disable path. Prioritized P2 alongside the model/provider/voice work for that reason.

## Standards references

- punt-kit/standards/cli.md §Core Principle, §Subcommand naming, §Global Flags, §Required Subcommands, §Projection Strategy
- punt-kit/standards/tool-enable-disable.md §2.3, §2.14 (mandates /vox enable / /vox disable, no colon-namespace)
- punt-kit/standards/python.md Rule 5 (Humble Object Commands / commands/ layer)

## History and superseded work

- DES-060 (accepted) mandated enablement stays under /vox — this epic upholds it, only removes model/provider from /vox
- vox-cnak: closed and split into 4 sibling tasks under this epic
- vox-yn8u: CHANGELOG-cited follow-up to rename mic:unmute + /unmute in lockstep with vox say — the mic:unmute strip-overloads task under this epic completes that intent

## Out of scope

- vox-mof0 / vox-donx: music CLI/MCP module decomposition — module-layout work, not user-facing UX
- vox-yn8u (as a separate bead): the CLI rename shipped in vox-2vto; the MCP/slash side lands as part of the mic:unmute cleanup task here — the bead intent is fully covered

title: VoxClient/VoxClientSync drift is real: fetch_part exists on async only, and no test compares the surfaces
description:
Found while reviewing vox-w3f8 PR 2 (2026-08-14). Not a defect today; a gap that guarantees one later.

`VoxClientSync` mirrors `VoxClient`'s async methods through a generic Callable-factory bridge (`_drive`). PR 2 added 21 dispatch tests using `AsyncMock(spec=VoxClient)`, which enforces the real signature — a lambda passing wrong keywords or arity fails at await. That closes argument drift for the methods that exist.

It does NOT close SURFACE drift. There is no assertion that every public method on VoxClient has a counterpart on VoxClientSync. A method added to the async client and forgotten in the sync one is invisible: no test fails, no type checker complains, and the omission only surfaces when a CLI, hook, or panel caller reaches for a method that is not there.

This matters more than it looks because VoxClientSync is the client EVERY non-async surface uses — CLI, hooks, panel, and the MCP server's sync paths. The async/sync pair is a maintenance obligation nothing currently enforces.

PROPOSED: one test asserting the public method sets correspond.

    def test_sync_client_mirrors_every_async_method():
        async_methods = {m for m in dir(VoxClient) if not m.startswith('_') and callable(...)}
        sync_methods  = {m for m in dir(VoxClientSync) if not m.startswith('_') and callable(...)}
        assert async_methods - sync_methods == set()   # or an explicit documented exclusion set

An explicit exclusion set is better than a bare equality if some async methods legitimately have no sync counterpart — the exclusions then have to be written down and justified, which is the point.

CONTEXT: gvr raised this themselves in PR 2's handoff, under a 'what the evidence does not cover' section, having been asked to state what their verification did NOT establish. Filing rather than folding it into that PR: it is a new test for an existing gap, not a defect in the change under review.
notes:
VALIDATED 2026-08-15 against main (9b9eaba), post vox-w3f8 PR 2.

Still real. PR 2 added 22 tests pinning every VoxClientSync method to its wire
frame and took that file to 100% coverage -- but those tests pin sync-to-wire,
NOT sync-to-async. Nothing asserts the two surfaces stay in step, which is
exactly what this bead says.

MEASURED DRIFT AS OF TODAY:

  uv run python -c "import inspect, punt_vox.client as a, punt_vox.client_sync as s; ..."
  async-only: ['close', 'connect', 'fetch_part']
  sync-only : []
  shared    : 24

close/connect are lifecycle and legitimately async-only -- any parity test must
exempt them explicitly rather than by accident.

fetch_part is the real finding. It is PUBLIC by name but INTERNAL by use: the
only caller is client.py:889, another async method on the same class. So it is
either (a) mis-named and should be _fetch_part, which makes the parity gap
vanish, or (b) a genuine sync-surface gap where a sync caller cannot fetch an
album part. Resolve which before writing the test, because the test's exemption
list encodes the answer.

Note the shape: 24 methods agree and the tests are green on both sides, and the
one asymmetry is invisible because no test compares the surfaces at all. Same
class as the other defects found on 2026-08-14/15 -- green everywhere, nothing
looking at the thing that matters.

title: Python API surface audit: name the failures, type the returns, document the lifecycle
description:
Per-surface audit toward vox-iyqq. rmh audited the Python client (VoxClient async in client.py + VoxClientSync in client_sync.py). Finding 1 (clients not top-level exported) is FIXED on branch docs/reposition-surfaces — VoxClient, VoxClientSync, SynthesisSpec, SynthesizeResult now in punt_vox/__all__ with a test — pending the coupling-ratchet resolution. Remaining findings, ranked:

2. [biggest] Exception types are unexported and have no common base. VoxdConnectionError + VoxdProtocolError (client_errors.py:6,10) are what a caller must catch around connect/synthesize/record, but they are NOT in the package __all__ (a third party imports from the non-public punt_vox.client_errors), and both subclass Exception directly with no shared VoxError base — so a caller cannot write one 'except VoxError'. A public client whose failure modes cannot be named from the public namespace. Add a VoxError base; export both + the base.

3. program_* and health return raw dict at the public boundary. VoxClient.health() -> dict[str, object] (client.py:407) and every program_* method returns dict[str, Any] (client.py:429-482, mirrored in client_sync.py). A caller cannot discover the response shape from the type (violates PY-OO-4/PY-TS-14). SynthesizeResult is a proper frozen dataclass (good model); status/health/program have no equivalent. Add typed result dataclasses (e.g. ProgramStatus, HealthStatus).

4. PromptSet (a program_on/program_select argument, client.py:439) is an unexported internal type (punt_vox.music_prompts.PromptSet). To drive the program surface with authored prompts a caller must import a non-public module. Export PromptSet or accept a public type.

5. No documented third-party usage example. tests/test_public_api.py now covers the import path, but there is no end-to-end connect -> synthesize/record -> close example in README/docs. Add one (dovetails with vox-iyqq's 'Ways to use vox' section).

6. Docstrings leak internals / omit the lifecycle contract. VoxClient's class docstring (client.py:289) describes 'composing a _VoxdTransport' (impl detail); neither client documents the 'call connect() once before sending' contract at the class level, nor that VoxClientSync connects per-call. Rewrite the class docstrings for the API consumer.

7. Sync/async parity — VERIFIED COHERENT, not an issue. VoxClientSync wraps all of VoxClient's RPC methods at matching signatures; omits only connect/close by design (fresh connection per call).

CLOSURE: 2 + 3 are the substance — a public client should let you NAME its failures and TYPE its returns. Requested by Jim 2026-07-11.

## Context
Third of three per-surface audits for vox-iyqq. Finding 1 (export) done on branch but blocked by the coupling-ratchet deadlock — see the separate decision.
close_reason: Python API surface audit shipped. Finding 1 (client export) was already on main (#315). Findings 2-6 done: VoxError base + exported exception hierarchy; health()/program_* now return typed frozen dataclasses (HealthStatus, ProgramStatus, CommandOutcome, ProgramSummary) instead of raw dict; PromptSet exported; both client docstrings rewritten + VoxClient async context manager; README end-to-end example. Review-round fixes: wire-parse ValueError wrapped as VoxdProtocolError so the 'every failure is a VoxError' contract holds; CommandOutcome documented honestly (Phase-1 acks at enqueue, applied always True); the client's coupling to the daemon was eliminated by extracting the wire types to a neutral types_programs package (import punt_vox now pulls ZERO voxd modules + zero heavy deps, verified by test) which collapsed the 3 coupling waivers and restored the client=stdlib+websockets boundary. Real command-rejection reachability is vox-wywa. make check green (2534 tests).

title: vox daemon has no stop or start, only restart
description:
The daemon subcommand exposes restart but no stop and no start, so there is no way to bring voxd down and leave it down, or to bring it up without first bringing it down.

Consequences:
  - Verifying a freshly installed build takes a restart, which conflates two
    operations: you cannot confirm the old process is gone before the new one
    starts, and a failure in either half reports as one outcome.
  - Nothing can stop the daemon for a maintenance window, a port conflict, or
    to hand the audio device to something else, short of killing the process
    by pid.
  - install/uninstall already have their own verbs; the running/stopped state
    does not.

Wanted: 'vox daemon stop' and 'vox daemon start' alongside restart, each
reporting what it actually did (already stopped / already running are normal
outcomes, not errors), with restart composed from the two rather than
duplicating either.

Note the service backends differ -- launchd on macOS, systemd on Linux -- so
this lands in service/ behind the existing backend seam, not in the CLI.

title: vox --json inconsistent: trailing form fails on rec/music sub-apps + wrong rec-list docstring
description: vox --json is rejected in the TRAILING position across ALL rec and music sub-app commands (operator-confirmed: 'vox rec ... --json' and 'vox music ... --json' -> 'No such option: --json', exit 2). Top-level commands accept trailing --json (cli_io.py routes both 'vox --json status' and 'vox status --json'); the sub-apps do not, so the whole rec/music machine-readable surface is inconsistent. Workaround that DOES work: the global position -- 'vox --json rec list' emits proper JSON ({recordings:[{id,bytes}]}). Also cli_rec.py:245 docstring 'one per line (--json for bytes)' is wrong. Fix: route trailing --json on every rec/music sub-app command for parity with top-level, and correct the docstring. Domain: CLI (mdm worker / rop evaluator). Found smoke-testing v4.14.0.
close_reason: Duplicate of vox-cnak — folded the --json trailing-form breakage (rec/music sub-apps) and the wrong rec-list docstring into vox-cnak, which was bumped to P2.

title: EPIC: daemon is the audio host — route all client audio/state ops through voxd
description:
Audit 2026-07-21 (agent, read-only) of every client path that bypasses voxd or assumes a local daemon. The remote transport itself is clean: VoxClient/VoxClientSync dial VOXD_HOST/PORT/TOKEN (client_env.py:34-60, client.py:166-173); everything over the socket works remote. The gaps are the commands that do work in the client process instead of over the socket — so on a remote daemon they touch the wrong machine.

SEQUENCE AFTER vox-tnum. tnum's RecordHandler (daemon-side handler + wire op, client sends a request and the daemon does the work) is the template every child copies; once it lands the rest are mostly mechanical — 'correct almost by default' (operator, 2026-07-21).

SETTLED (not an open decision, despite the audit re-raising it): record/recording output lands on the DAEMON host (daemon owns audio files), labeled host:path when the daemon is remote (vox-eoq9). Playback likewise routes through the daemon (vox-ovb7).

## Category A — must route through the daemon (broken when remote), by impact
- A1 vox play (__main__.py:941-951 -> playback.py:50): spawns afplay/ffplay in the CLIENT process. Plays on client speakers, never the daemon host. => vox-ovb7 (filed).
- A2 vox record (__main__.py:442-450): client.record() bytes over wire, then CLI write_bytes client-side under ~/Music/vox. => vox-tnum (in flight).
- A3 MCP record tool (server.py:575-577 -> recording.py:46): same, RecordingSink writes on the MCP-server machine; returned path names the client fs. => vox-tnum.
- A4 vox cache status/clear (__main__.py:959-989 -> cache.py:150,173): operate on the LOCAL ~/.punt-labs/vox/cache, not the daemon's. On a remote daemon, clear silently no-ops and status reports the client's empty cache. => new child bead.
- A5 vox daemon status (__main__.py:1070-1107): reads the local port file + hardcodes http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health, ignoring VOXD_HOST — inconsistent with vox status / vox doctor which use client.health(). => new child bead (mechanical).

## Category B — client-local, ambiguous on a remote daemon (P4, enumerate then file when worked)
- vox log (__main__.py:542-565): writes client ~/.punt-labs/vox/; a remote daemon reads its own home, so daemon verbosity never changes from the client.
- MCP status vox.log health (server.py:922-923 -> vibe_trace.py:57 + log_health): post-299b495 vox.log is one log incl. voxd; on a remote daemon status reports the CLIENT's vox.log, not the daemon's (which lives on the remote host).
- default_output_dir (dirs.py:86, server.py:362): ~/Music/vox resolves on whichever machine runs the code; once record moves daemon-side it must resolve on the DAEMON. Coupled to tnum/eoq9.
- vox doctor (doctor.py:104-293): ffmpeg/music-dir/output-dir/uvx/espeak/python checks inspect the CLIENT; audio plays + files land on the daemon host, so doctor can report all-green while the daemon host lacks ffmpeg. (daemon-health + VOXD_* override checks correctly go through the client.)
- Legitimately local (leave): install/install-desktop/uninstall + daemon install/uninstall/restart drive the local launchctl/systemctl and cannot manage a remote daemon; vibe/notify/speak/voice config writes are consumed client-side before the wire call.

## Category C — already correct (through voxd)
vox say, MCP unmute, vox voices / MCP who, vox status daemon fields / MCP status program block, vox music (all of cli_music.py + MCP music*), all hooks (stop/notification/continuous/_chime), vox doctor daemon-health + VOXD_* reporting.

Children: vox-ovb7 (A1 play), vox-tnum (A2/A3 record), vox-eoq9 (remote host:path label), + new A4 (cache) and A5 (daemon status) beads, + the Category B P4 items above filed when the epic is worked.

title: voxd dies at boot on a bad SSL_CERT_FILE because the music provider builds its HTTPS client eagerly
description:
Found on macOS by claude:tty13 while verifying PR #490 (ecb2043).

REPRO: export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/that/does/not/exist, then start voxd.
Daemon dies at boot with an uncaught FileNotFoundError. Speech, chimes, hooks
and every non-music path go down with it.

CHAIN:
  daemon.py:236          _build_programs() -> MusicProducer(ElevenLabsMusicProvider(), ...)
  elevenlabs_music.py:53 __new__ -> ElevenLabs(api_key=key), eagerly
  (SDK)                  builds an httpx client, which calls
                         ssl.create_default_context(cafile=os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'])
                         at construction -> FileNotFoundError, uncaught

So SSL_CERT_FILE is not read lazily per-request. A wrong or stale CA path is a
total daemon outage at startup, unconditionally, for users who never touch
music. A music provider should not be able to stop the daemon from speaking.

WHY IT IS NOT A #490 REGRESSION: the workaround #490 replaces -- a launchctl
bootout/bootstrap cycle from an activation script -- injected SSL_CERT_FILE
into the same LaunchAgent, so this crash was already reachable for exactly the
users who need the var. #490 replaces a racy injection with a reliable one; it
does not newly expose the crash. Not held for the 5.0.4 release on that basis.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): the provider's client construction is eager in
__new__ at the composition root. Deferring it to first use would confine a bad
CA to the music path, where it can be surfaced as a music error instead of a
boot failure. Note elevenlabs.py:89 and elevenlabs_stt.py:86 construct clients
the same way -- check whether either is also on the boot path before choosing
where the fix belongs.

Whatever the shape, a bad CA path must not prevent voxd from starting, and the
failure must name SSL_CERT_FILE: an uncaught FileNotFoundError on a cafile is
not a diagnosable message for the operator who set that var.

title: test_voxd_daemon drives the real lifespan, so MusicPlayerSubsystem connects to the LIVE Lux hub
description:
The h7k8 fix stopped the TESTS from spawning real vox-panels. This is the same defect class one layer down, in the daemon, and h7k8 did not touch it -- which is why the phantom album row is still appearing after that fix merged.

CHAIN:
  tests/test_voxd_daemon.py:91,114   async with daemon._lifespan(app)
  src/punt_vox/voxd/daemon.py:170    MusicPlayerSubsystem(service, service.changes)
                                     <- TWO args; the third (clients) defaults
  music_player/composition.py:56     clients if clients is not None else VoxLuxClients()
                                     <- the REAL factory, resolving luxd's real port
  -> connects to the live hub on 8430
  -> publishes a vox.music scene built from the test's tmp_path/'programs' store

Two tests do it: test_lifespan_starts_tasks_and_applies_a_command and
test_lifespan_cancels_tasks_on_exit. The module docstring states the intent
plainly -- 'This drives the real lifespan context' -- so the lux connection is
incidental, not intended: the tests are about background-task wiring and inject
a ProgramSubsystem with a fake producer. Nobody noticed the lifespan also
composes the music player with production clients.

WHY THIS IS THE MISSING PIECE: every other candidate was ruled out by
measurement.
  - the album store holds exactly 4 albums, none named 'mix'
  - src/ contains no literal that display_title() could render as 'Mix'
    (an album whose name tag is 'mix' or 'mix-<stamp>' titles as exactly 'Mix';
     an unnamed album titles as 'Album')
  - the real voxd NEVER logged rendering 'Mix' -- only receiving CLICKS on it
    (vox.log, 2026-08-29 15:51 and 2026-08-30 14:48)
  - only one voxd process and one voxd hub connection exist
  - every MusicPlayerSubsystem in tests/music_player injects _FakeClients, and
    test_lux_clients monkeypatches HubPaths.read_port to 8080/9090
  - vox-panel renders no album table (panel/ has no album code)
So the only remaining producer of a vox.music scene is this one.

Note VOX_OUTPUT_DIR overrides the store root (dirs.py:93), so a test-scoped
store is what such a connection would publish -- the rows need not exist on the
real disk, which is why the row was never findable there.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): the lifespan should not be able to reach
production clients from a test. Injecting the client factory into VoxDaemon --
so the composition root, not _lifespan, decides -- would make it structural
rather than a matter of remembering. A regression test should assert that
driving the lifespan opens no connection to luxd's real port; asserting on the
tmp store alone would not have caught this.

Same family as vox-h7k8 (hook tests spawning panels) and vox-y73x (leaked
panel pid files). Worth auditing for any OTHER production client a test-driven
lifespan composes.
close_reason: Fixed in #494 (318fb56). The lux client factory is now a VoxDaemon constructor argument, so a test driving the real lifespan cannot reach production clients. The phantom row was this test module's own turn_on(style='techno', name='mix') published to the live hub.

title: Conversation Mode — Phase 1
description:
A human can hold a live voice conversation with their own, already-running Claude Code session through vox -- hands and eyes free, wearing headphones, ElevenLabs configured -- that they would genuinely choose over typing.

Source design: docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex (two chapters, revised after five live spikes and two independent design reviews). Slice plan: .tmp/conversation-mode-epic-slices.md (revised after independent review of the plan itself).

Definition of done: all child beads closed, the Phase 1 audio-demo flight (docs/WORKFLOW.md) run and confirmed by ear, and all three operator-reserved design forks (session-attach shape, PlaybackQueue architecture, presence-pool mechanism) explicitly ratified by the operator -- not merely resolved inside a mission.

Explicitly deferred past Phase 1 (not silently dropped): mid-call self-correction, developer debug log for a live call. Revisit at Phase 1 close.

Session-attach mechanism: RATIFIED as specified in docs/conversation-mode-session-attach-adr.md -- claude -p --resume per turn. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-23/24: implemented, shipped in Slice 1b, confirmed unworkable by real measurement (DES-065, 13-25s median latency per turn). Replaced by fork 4's mechanism, now itself ratified -- see below. 2. Continuous-stream playback ownership: RATIFIED -- built directly into production PlaybackQueue. Still stands. 3. Presence-signal mechanism: RATIFIED -- the static-asset path outside the Program state machine. Still stands. FOURTH OPERATOR-RESERVED DESIGN FORK: RATIFIED 2026-08-24 (vox-m2ss, closed). FR-4's revised wording (docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex): the replacement mechanism (vox-hobl, spike-confirmed, DESIGN.md DES-066/DES-067) satisfies FR-4's intent via a context snapshot taken at call start, not a literal resume of the primary session's live state. Operator: 'yes, I sign off on context snapshot not literal session resume.' ALL FOUR FORKS NOW RATIFIED. Slice 1b (vox-gs9u.2) remains held open pending vox-hobl.2 landing and a re-run audio-demo gate against the new implementation -- see vox-gs9u.2's own description.

title: Slice 1b: One real round trip
description:
End-to-end capability: run vox call start (CLI) or /call start (slash command), ask one real question by voice, get one real spoken answer from the user's actual, already-running Claude Code session -- not the authoring session standing in for it, not a mocked agent.

In scope:
- vox call start (CLI) / /call start (slash command) trigger -- no hotkey
- Turn detection (accumulated-run model, calibrated at call start -- not fixed thresholds tuned once in one room)
- ElevenLabs STT
- The SessionAttach Protocol boundary (src/punt_vox/voxd/conversation_mode/session_attach.py) and one working implementation of it. SUPERSEDED (2026-08-24): the original implementation this slice built (ClaudeSessionAttach, a headless claude -p --resume subprocess per human turn, per the now-superseded session-attach ADR) is confirmed unworkable by real measurement -- see DESIGN.md DES-065 (13-25s median latency per turn). It is replaced by the mechanism designed and spike-confirmed in vox-hobl (a persistent pi --mode rpc call agent, held alive for the whole call). The Protocol boundary itself does not change; only the implementation behind it does. This slice is NOT done until that replacement implementation lands and the audio-demo gate is run against it -- running the gate against the old ClaudeSessionAttach would confirm a UX the epic's own bar already rejects.
- A full (non-streamed) reply from that session
- ElevenLabs TTS played back
- Audible state cues for "listening" and "here's the reply" via mic:unmute per NFR-6, built in from the start (cheap now, expensive to retrofit)
- Call timeout (FR-2) and basic hangup (vox call stop / /call stop)
- Provider interface boundary (FR-21) defined generically even though only ElevenLabs implements it -- first place STT/TTS get wired, last cheap point to get the boundary shape right
- Never fabricate on ambiguous or failed capture (FR-19) -- ask the human to repeat rather than act on a low-confidence transcript

Explicitly out of scope: barge-in, presence signal, sentence-streamed synthesis (reply spoken as one block), graceful degradation beyond "the call doesn't start."

All three ORIGINAL operator-reserved design forks are ratified (session-attach mechanism as originally scoped, playback-ownership, presence-signal) -- see epic notes. A NEW operator-reserved fork has since opened (FR-4's revised wording, per vox-hobl and docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex) and blocks the replacement implementation from dispatching, though it does not block the retained mic/STT/turn-detection/lock work this slice already delivered.

Retained from the existing branch (does not need rework): MicAudioSource, ElevenLabsSTTProvider, TurnDetector, CallLock/CallControl, LiveCallDriver's mic-echo gating, CallSession orchestration, turn-timer diagnostics. Replaced: ClaudeSessionAttach, ClaudeSubprocessEnv's --bare/keep_api_key variant, SessionDiscovery -- these implemented SessionAttach against the old mechanism only.

Source: docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex Chapters 1-2; docs/conversation-mode-session-attach-adr.md (superseded mechanism); DESIGN.md DES-065/DES-066 (what failed, what replaces it); docs/conversation-mode-call-agent.tex (Z spec for the replacement process lifecycle); .tmp/conversation-mode-epic-slices.md
