SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-08-22, post-dispatch): no hotkey trigger needed. The
trigger is `vox call start` (CLI) / `/call start` (slash command), per the
ratified command naming in docs/conversation-mode-session-attach-adr.md.
Drop any hotkey-listener requirement from this slice.

title: Slice 2a: Playback-ownership (ratified: extend PlaybackQueue directly)
description:
RATIFIED: build continuous-stream playback ownership directly into production PlaybackQueue (not a new sibling component). This was operator-ratified 2026-08-22 -- see epic notes. This bead's remaining scope is the design/implementation work under that already-decided direction, not producing or escalating a recommendation.

Remaining scope: resolve the concurrency-ordering questions the design chapter explicitly leaves open: what happens when a barge-in stop-signal races with natural turn-completion; what happens if a second barge-in fires while the first stop's buffer-clear is still in flight; from what thread is the buffer cleared, under what lock, relative to the writer thread feeding synthesized audio into the same stream. Feed the answer into the Slice 1a Z spec's transition model.

Source: docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex Chapter 2, "Barge-in and its two latencies" and "Decisions required before implementation" item 2.
notes:
TESTABILITY ADDENDUM (Chapter 3 test-plan review):

The in-memory playback-sink fake this slice's design must specify is necessary but NOT sufficient on its own for the concurrency-ordering questions this slice resolves (stop-during-a-stop, buffer-clear racing a concurrent writer thread). A fake that just records calls, driven single-threadedly, proves nothing about a race that only exists when two call sites contend.

Required: pair the in-memory sink with an actual concurrency/interleaving harness -- controlled asyncio task scheduling with deterministic yield points, or a threaded stress test run N times -- that drives the race for real. This harness is part of this slice's design-phase deliverable, not a follow-on.
SEQUENCING (per epic goal: test infra built before/during dev, never at the end):

This design bead's deliverable now explicitly INCLUDES building, not just specifying, the playback-sink Protocol, its in-memory fake, AND the concurrency/interleaving harness that actually drives the stop-during-a-stop / buffer-clear-vs-writer race. All three must exist and have passing tests proving the chosen ordering discipline holds BEFORE this bead closes. Slice 2b (implementation) starts against already-working test infra, not a design note it has to operationalize itself.

title: vox call: design investigation — persistent, parallel call agent (not spawned per turn)
description:
Design investigation, decided 2026-08-23 after live latency testing.
Per-turn subprocess spawn (the ratified ADR Option D) is confirmed too
slow for real conversation -- median 13-25s wall clock per turn even with
zero context, dominated by process startup, not model latency (see
vox-eu5q, vox-qw1x, vox-gkym, and the 20-run claude-vs-pi benchmark in
vox-36xc's description). This bead is the longer-term fix; vox-36xc is
the near-term patch to make the current design tolerable while this was
investigated.

MECHANISM DECIDED AND SPIKE-CONFIRMED (2026-08-24) -- see DESIGN.md
DES-066 for the full evidence trail:

- One persistent `pi --mode rpc --no-session --no-extensions` process,
  spawned once at call start, held alive for the whole call via a direct
  `subprocess.Popen` in `voxd` itself (not tmux/pi-tools' `keep`
  extension -- avoids a new runtime dependency for a headless-daemon use
  case `keep` was not built for). NOT claude -- pi's minimal-bootstrap
  design (no MCP, no plugin ecosystem by default) is what makes the
  persistence win real; the claude-vs-pi comparison this bead originally
  left open is resolved in favor of pi.
- Persistence verified live: one process held across two sequential
  turns, replied correctly to both, second turn reused first turn's warm
  context (cacheRead evidence).
- Real tool-use latency verified live: a cold turn including an actual
  file-read tool call reached first spoken text at 6.8s, completed at
  7.0s; a warm follow-up completed 4.3s later -- an order of magnitude
  under the 13-25s per-turn-spawn median, and that number did zero tool
  use.
- Read-only enforcement: pi's native `--tools read,grep,find,ls` CLI
  allowlist (confirmed against pi's own docs). Verified live: a prompted
  write was never attempted by the model at all with only that allowlist
  set.

REQUIRED SCOPE, NOT OPTIONAL (found during security review, spike-verified
2026-08-24):

- The `--tools` allowlist blocks writes, not disclosure. Verified live: a
  fake secret dropped into a probe file was read and narrated back
  verbatim by the agent -- in production this becomes spoken audio in a
  room. The implementation MUST include either an explicit deny-list of
  sensitive paths (`.env*`, this repo's own `.gitignore` secret patterns)
  enforced before the call agent can read them, or an explicit, documented
  decision to accept the residual risk. Silence is not an option.
- `subprocess.Popen` inherits the parent env by default; `voxd` already
  holds provider API keys (ElevenLabs/OpenAI/AWS) in its own env. The
  call-agent spawn MUST strip these before launch, the same discipline
  `ClaudeSubprocessEnv` already applies to `claude` subprocesses
  (`src/punt_vox/voxd/conversation_mode/claude_subprocess_env.py`) --
  this is not a follow-on fix, it goes in the same commit as the spawn
  code.

STILL UNDESIGNED (blocking an implementation mission from dispatching):

1. The context-snapshot's own content and construction -- what actually
   goes into the call agent's opening message (current task, relevant
   files, recent conversation gist per the original proposal, but the
   concrete shape is not designed).
2. The post-call summary handoff to the primary session -- mechanism
   (file the primary session's next `UserPromptSubmit` hook reads?
   injected context block? something else?) is not designed.

OPERATOR-RESERVED FORK, NOT YET RATIFIED:

`docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex` FR-4 has been revised (2026-08-24) to
name explicitly that this mechanism satisfies FR-4's intent (task context
carried into the call) but not its original literal wording (the call
agent is the *same session*) -- the call agent now starts fresh with a
context snapshot, deliberately disconnected from the primary session's
live state. This is a genuine architecture fork from FR-4 as originally
written and needs explicit operator ratification before an implementation
mission dispatches, per this project's own design-review discipline
(CLAUDE.md / docs/WORKFLOW.md) -- not something to build mid-investigation.

A Z spec for the call-agent process lifecycle already exists and passes
fuzz type-checking: `docs/conversation-mode-call-agent.tex`.

Once FR-4 is ratified and the two still-undesigned pieces above are
designed, this converts from a design investigation into an
implementation mission against `vox-gs9u.2`'s existing `SessionAttach`
Protocol boundary -- `ClaudeSessionAttach` is replaced by a new
implementation of the same interface; the mic/STT/turn-detection/lock
layers `vox-gs9u.2` already built are unaffected.

title: Design the call-agent context-snapshot content and post-call summary handoff
description:
The two pieces DES-066/vox-hobl explicitly leave undesigned, and the only remaining work before the replacement SessionAttach implementation can be scoped as a mission:

1. CONTEXT-SNAPSHOT CONTENT -- RESOLVED (2026-08-24), operator direction: entry point is `/vox:call start <topic>`. The PRIMARY session (the one the human is already working in, and is the one that types the slash command) constructs the opening context snapshot handed to the call agent, not the call agent itself and not an automated extraction pass. This directly resolves the "sourced from where" question: the primary session already has the current task, recent conversation, and repo state in its own context -- it authors the snapshot from what it already knows plus <topic>, the same way any handoff between two collaborators would work.

   RESEARCH DONE ON QUARRY/CONTEXT7 ACCESS, MCP APPROACH REJECTED (2026-08-24): initially explored giving the call agent live tool access to quarry (semantic search over source + conversation history) and context7 (docs) via pi's third-party `pi-mcp-adapter` extension. Spiked (`-e <path> --no-extensions`) and found the `--tools` allowlist filters extension-registered tools too, not just built-ins, so the mcp-adapter's own tool was invisible to the model even when the extension itself loaded successfully. OPERATOR REJECTED this direction outright before further debugging: "I do not wish or need to use mcp with pi... do not bloat pi." Do not revisit MCP-in-pi for this feature.

   RESOLVED MECHANISM instead: quarry access happens in the PRIMARY session, before the call agent is even spawned. `quarry --json find "<query>"` is a real, working CLI flag (verified live, 2026-08-24) -- the primary session runs it against a query derived from <topic>, and folds relevant hits directly into the context-snapshot text. Same pattern applies to context7 if a topic clearly needs external docs -- the primary session looks it up and bakes the result in, rather than granting the call agent live tool access. The call agent's own tool surface stays exactly `--tools read,grep,find,ls`, `--no-extensions`, unchanged from DES-066 -- this whole mechanism adds ZERO new tools or extensions to the spawned pi process, all the extra context-gathering happens upstream, in Python, in voxd/the primary session.

2. SUMMARY-HANDOFF MECHANISM -- content format RESOLVED (2026-08-24), delivery mechanism still open. Operator direction: model the post-call summary on `../prfaq/`'s meeting-summary format (see `../prfaq/meetings/meeting-summary-*.md` for the reference shape) -- a structured document, not free prose: Decisions Made, Action Items (what the primary session should do next -- this IS the handoff), Context Gathered (files read, quarry hits, docs consulted), Beads Touched, Notes/Open Questions. Since the call is started FROM the primary session (`/vox:call start`), the simplest delivery mechanism is that the primary session itself, still present, reads the summary file directly when the call ends -- no UserPromptSubmit hook injection needed, unlike the original candidate list assumed a scenario where the primary session might not still be attached. STILL OPEN: the exact file location/naming convention, and whether the call agent itself authors the summary (via its own final turn) or the primary session synthesizes it from the raw call transcript after the fact -- author recommends the former (the call agent is closest to what happened) with the primary session free to add its own notes on read.

Output: a short design note (ADR-style, in DESIGN.md alongside DES-065/066, or a new DES-06N entry) naming the chosen mechanism for each and the rejected alternatives (including the rejected MCP-in-pi approach above, so it is not re-attempted). Does not require FR-4 ratification (vox-m2ss) to start -- this is a design question independent of whether the snapshot approach itself is ratified -- but the FOLLOW-ON IMPLEMENTATION does require it.

title: Implement the persistent call-agent SessionAttach replacement (pi --mode rpc), with required security hardening
description:
Replaces ClaudeSessionAttach (src/punt_vox/voxd/conversation_mode/claude_session_attach.py) with a new implementation of the same SessionAttach Protocol (src/punt_vox/voxd/conversation_mode/session_attach.py), per the mechanism spike-confirmed in DESIGN.md DES-066:

1. One pi --mode rpc --no-session --no-extensions process, spawned once at call start, held alive for the whole call via a direct subprocess.Popen in voxd itself. Drive it over the documented stdin/stdout JSONL RPC protocol (prompt/steer/follow_up/abort in; message_update/agent_end out) directly -- not through pi-tools/tmux.
2. --tools read,grep,find,ls (no bash/edit/write) at process launch, per the call-agent's Z model (docs/conversation-mode-call-agent.tex): readOnly holds for the process's whole live extent, not toggled per turn.
3. REQUIRED, not optional (spike-verified security findings, DES-066): (a) an explicit deny-list of sensitive paths (.env*, this repo's own .gitignore secret patterns) enforced before the call agent can read them, or an explicit documented decision to accept the residual disclosure risk -- reading was spike-confirmed to narrate a fake secret's contents verbatim; (b) strip voxd's own provider API keys (ElevenLabs/OpenAI/AWS) from the spawned process's environment before launch, the same discipline ClaudeSubprocessEnv already applies to claude subprocesses.
4. CONTEXT-SNAPSHOT CONSTRUCTION, decided (DES-067): a new `/vox:call start <topic>` slash command whose prompt has the PRIMARY session (not voxd, not the call agent) author the opening context snapshot from <topic> plus its own current task/conversation context, folding in `quarry --json find "<query>"` hits (and context7 lookups if warranted) run by the primary session BEFORE the call agent spawns. This snapshot text is passed through to `vox call start` (a new CLI flag or equivalent transport -- not yet specified at the flag level) and becomes the call agent's opening message. The call agent's own tool surface is unaffected -- item 2 above stays exactly as scoped, zero new tools or extensions added to the spawned pi process.
5. SUMMARY-HANDOFF, decided (DES-067): a new `calls_dir()` helper in src/punt_vox/paths.py, alongside the existing `recordings_dir()` (same one-helper-per-purpose convention). The call agent authors the summary itself as its own final turn, before Teardown/AbortTurn, written to `calls_dir() / "<call-id>-summary.md"`. Format: a structured document modeled on ../prfaq/'s meeting-summary format (Decisions Made / Action Items / Context Gathered / Beads Touched / Notes/Open Questions) -- see DES-067 for the full section-by-section rationale. Delivery: the primary session (still present, since /vox:call start is not a detached invocation) reads the file directly when the call ends -- no UserPromptSubmit hook, no polling mechanism needed.
6. Satisfies the call-agent process lifecycle modeled in docs/conversation-mode-call-agent.tex (Spawn/SendTurn/ReplyComplete/Teardown/AbortTurn) -- tests should assert the modeled invariants by name.

Still open at the flag/wire-format level (small implementation details for this mission, not architectural forks): exactly how the primary session passes the constructed snapshot text to `vox call start` (inline arg vs. a temp file vs. stdin), and calls_dir()'s retention/cleanup policy.

Once this lands, re-run vox-gs9u.2's audio-demo gate against the new implementation -- do not close vox-gs9u.2 against the old ClaudeSessionAttach.

title: Ratify FR-4's revised wording: call agent gets a context snapshot, not a literal session resume
description:
docs/conversation-mode-prd.tex FR-4 originally required the call to use the user's active session, carrying its existing task context, not a fresh one. The mechanism that satisfies this without the 13-25s per-turn latency DES-065 confirmed unworkable (vox-hobl, DESIGN.md DES-066, spike-confirmed 2026-08-23/24) starts the call agent as a FRESH process at call start, handed a context SNAPSHOT (current task, relevant files, recent conversation gist) as its opening message -- deliberately disconnected from the primary session's live state, so a call cannot hang on a primary session that is mid-turn.

This satisfies FR-4's underlying intent (real task context, not a blank start) but not its literal original wording (the same session object). The PRD (FR-4, revised 2026-08-24) recommends ratifying this reading as an explicit, named exception rather than silently reinterpreting the requirement.

DECISION NEEDED: approve the context-snapshot reading of FR-4 (recommended -- the alternative, a literal resume, is the mechanism DES-065 already confirmed unworkable, so there is no faster alternative that keeps the literal wording), or reject it and send the mechanism back for a different design.

Blocks: the implementation mission for the replacement SessionAttach (see dependent bead).

title: opencode host support: native vox adapter
description: Epic: support opencode as a second host for vox. Smaller scope than the biff program (no trust model, no delivery policy) — the SAME engineering bar. This is not a pilot hack: it establishes the org pattern "tool = daemon + N host adapters," and whatever ships here becomes the template other repos copy. Full lifecycle applies: requirements doc first (vox counterpart to biff/docs/requirements-biffd-multihost.md, reviewed by operator), then design mission with leader review before implementation dispatch, then implementation with tests, CI, and Phase-3 verification through the real entry point (a live opencode session producing audible chime/narration, introspection-captured, operator-confirmed). Architectural invariants to be stated in the requirements: (1) voxd, providers, recordings/music store, config ownership, and the vox CLI are unchanged — the adapter contains delivery mechanics only, zero engine logic; (2) host adapters differ only in delivery, never in semantics; (3) .punt-labs/vox/enabled remains the single host-agnostic per-repo gate. Scope: opencode-vox npm package (Plugin export: session.idle -> chime/narrate with SDK-read recap replacing the Stop-hook ♪ continuation protocol; permission.asked and session.error -> chime; session.compacted -> vibe refresh; file.edited -> continuous-mode signal); native opencode tools backed by voxd (unmute, voice, vibe, music, rec, status) with argument/output parity with the mic MCP tools; vox enable detecting opencode and depositing the tools shim, commands, and opencode.json plugin entry; npm as a version-locked release channel shipping together with the existing channels; Bun in CI with real end-to-end coverage. Design decisions to be resolved in the design mission, not discovered in implementation: recap summarizer (heuristic vs SDK call) with its quality bar; mapping of notify levels (normal/continuous) onto the opencode event set; plugin lifecycle/daemon-connection ownership (shares biff SP-4 findings). Origin: opencode research session 2026-08-29. Cross-ref: biff-00v and biff/docs/requirements-biffd-multihost.md — biff depends on the same host-adapter pattern; keep the adapter contracts consistent across the two programs.
notes:
Requirements doc drafted on branch docs/requirements-voxd-multihost (worktree .claude/worktrees/docs-voxd-multihost, commit 62007a8), pending operator review before PR.
Requirements doc PR opened: punt-labs/vox#482 (Copilot review requested). Language audit per operator ruling passed with no changes needed on the vox doc.

title: vox say --provider X is broken for every provider but the configured one: state's model is validated against the override
description:
`vox say --provider <name>` fails for all four non-configured providers. Found
2026-08-15 when Jim asked whether AWS/Polly still works, since Polly takes no
model parameter.

REPRODUCTION, state = elevenlabs/eleven_v3, against main 9b9eaba:

  $ vox say "test" --provider polly
  Error: model 'eleven_v3' is not available for provider 'polly' (available: )
  $ vox say "test" --provider say
  Error: model 'eleven_v3' is not available for provider 'say' (available: )
  $ vox say "test" --provider espeak
  Error: model 'eleven_v3' is not available for provider 'espeak' (available: )
  $ vox say "test" --provider openai
  Error: model 'eleven_v3' is not available for provider 'openai'
        (available: tts-1, tts-1-hd, gpt-4o-mini-tts)

Four for four. Only the already-configured provider works, which makes the
--provider flag useless for its entire purpose.

CAUSE. SessionSpec.fill resolves provider and model INDEPENDENTLY
(src/punt_vox/session_spec.py:106). _resolve_provider takes the override;
_resolve_model, given no model override, falls through to state's model -- which
belongs to the PREVIOUS provider -- and then validates it against the NEW one.
It can only pass when both providers happen to share a model name.

The cascade invariant "changing the provider resets the model" is implemented in
mic:provider and in the panel's _commit_provider. It is absent from the per-call
override path, so the two ways of choosing a provider disagree.

Note this is NOT the modelless case the design anticipated. docs/provider-authority.md
§3.9 reasoned about an EMPTY model and correctly kept polly/say/espeak working.
The broken case is a STALE model -- populated, valid for its own provider, wrong
for this call. openai proves it: it has models and still fails.

FIX. When the provider is overridden and no model override is supplied, the model
must not come from state -- state's model is scoped to state's provider. Resolve
to None (provider default) instead. Same rule wherever a per-call provider
override exists: the CLI --provider, mic:unmute, mic:rec new, and the panel voice
preview.

REGRESSION TEST. Parameterise over all five providers: with state set to one
provider, a per-call override to each of the other four must succeed without a
model argument. That is the assertion nobody wrote -- every existing test either
overrides both or neither.

SEVERITY. P1: two of the four broken providers (say, espeak) are the platform
fallbacks, so the documented escape hatch when a paid provider is down does not
work either. Shipped in vox-w3f8 PR 1 (0843ddc), so it has been live since then.

title: vox play bypasses voxd — plays in the client process, so remote playback lands on the wrong machine
description:
Found 2026-07-21 while working vox-tnum. Verified in code, not assumed.

The 'vox play' command (__main__.py, def play) has one line of body: play_audio(audio_file). play_audio (playback.py) spawns afplay/ffplay via subprocess IN THE CLIENT PROCESS, flock-serialized. It never connects to voxd.

Consequence in the remote/SSH scenario (client on host-b via VOXD_HOST -> daemon on host-a, the user's laptop with speakers): vox play runs the player on host-b (the dev box) — headless => error, or it plays where the user is not sitting. It never reaches host-a where the user actually hears audio.

This is inconsistent with the rest of vox: say, the chimes, hooks, and music all route THROUGH voxd and play on the daemon host — that is the whole reason a user on a remote box hears their agent on their laptop. vox play is the one audio command that bypasses the daemon.

Fix direction: route vox play through voxd so playback happens on the daemon host, consistent with say/chimes/music. The daemon opens and plays the file on ITS filesystem (the file already lives daemon-side under the emerging model: record writes there per vox-tnum candidate C; cache and tracks live there). Preserve local behavior: when daemon == client (loopback), it still plays on your one machine as today.

TRANSPORT CONSISTENCY: do NOT have the client stream file bytes to the daemon to play — that reintroduces the exact 1 MiB frame wall vox-tnum fixes, now on the play path. The daemon should read a path on its own filesystem (no bytes over the wire), matching vox-tnum's candidate C. If a file that lives on the CLIENT ever needs to play on the daemon, that is a separate transfer concern, not this bead.

This is the linchpin of the coherent 'daemon is the audio host' model: record writes daemon-side (vox-tnum), play reads+plays daemon-side (this bead), remote just labels the path (vox-eoq9). Blocks the 'how to play a remote recording' part of vox-eoq9.
close_reason: Resolved by vox-jei3 (#363): forward-integration deleted the top-level 'vox play' (verified post-release: 'vox play' -> No such command 'play', exit 2). Local files now use the OS player (afplay/ffplay) per guide-remote-setup.md; store recordings play on the daemon host via 'vox rec play', which routes through voxd. The bypassing command no longer exists, so the daemon-is-audio-host model holds.

title: Version skew between a running MCP server and the installed build is invisible — and WORKFLOW.md says a daemon restart is enough
description:
Hit three times on 2026-08-15, diagnosed from scratch each time.

WHAT HAPPENS. `vox mcp` is a stdio subprocess Claude Code spawns per session
(.claude-plugin/plugin.json). Its Python code is frozen at spawn. `make install`
replaces the package and `vox daemon restart` restarts voxd -- neither touches a
running MCP server. So a live session keeps calling yesterday's code against
today's daemon, silently.

THE THREE INSTANCES.
  1. Two vox-panel processes from before an install kept calling the pre-PR-2
     voices() signature. The upgraded daemon required an explicit provider and
     rejected them: `Unknown provider ''`. The panel showed an empty voice
     dropdown with no indication why. Killed the stale panels; symptom gone.
  2. After installing vox-w3f8 PR 3, `vox doctor` showed the new per-provider
     readiness section (fresh CLI process) while `mic:status` did not carry the
     new provider_status block (session's MCP server predates the install). Read
     as a defect in the PR until I checked the installed file and found the code
     present.
  3. The deposited agent guide had rotted the same way -- fixed separately as
     vox-prfr, which is the same idea: make drift visible.

THE DOC GAP, and it is what actually misled me. docs/WORKFLOW.md instructs
`make install` + `vox daemon restart` before exercising any MCP/hook/synthesis
path, and CLAUDE.md repeats it. That is true for synthesis and false for MCP. I
followed the documented procedure and got a wrong answer about a PR under review.

FIX, two parts:
  * docs/WORKFLOW.md + CLAUDE.md: state plainly that an MCP path additionally
    requires restarting the Claude session, because the mic server is spawned per
    session and holds its code in memory.
  * Surface the drift instead of leaving it to be deduced: the MCP server knows
    its own version and can read the installed package version. Report a mismatch
    through `mic:status` and `vox doctor` -- "this session's mic server is older
    than the installed build; restart the session." Same principle as vox-prfr's
    guide stamp: a silent staleness becomes one line of output.

NOT AN ARCHITECTURE PROBLEM. Per-session stdio is deliberate. mcp-proxy was the
previous design (DES-021) and DES-028 removed it on purpose, naming "the entire
class of 'MCP session doesn't survive daemon restart' bugs" as one of the things
elimination bought. Reintroducing a proxy would trade this problem for that one.
Jim raised the proxy option 2026-08-15; this is the recorded answer.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-15, same day. The 'NOT AN ARCHITECTURE PROBLEM' paragraph in the description is WRONG and I am striking it. Jim pushed back and he is right.

I answered a question he did not ask ('does mcp-proxy fix this staleness bug?') and used DES-028 as a reason not to think. That an ADR removed something once is precedent, not analysis -- and that removal was escaping a different problem (the v2 daemon resolving CWDs from PIDs).

His argument is that our code's lifecycle should not be owned by the Claude process. The standard we already adopted agrees. punt-kit/standards/architecture.md, invariant 4: 'Client-specific state lives in the engine, keyed by client... A client carries only its own identity and the context it alone can originate.' quarry is cited as the reference implementation; the quarry serve daemon holds each client's selected database, not the client.

DES-028 states vox's violation plainly: 'MCP server: Lightweight stdio process per Claude Code session. Session state in memory.' SessionConfig holds ten fields -- notify, speak, voice, provider, model, vibe_mode, vibe, vibe_tags, speak_explicit, session_id -- inside a process Claude owns and can kill.

THIS ALREADY CAUSED A SECOND BUG, and I misdiagnosed that one too. On the morning of 2026-08-15 Jim's provider/voice changed under him mid-session (elevenlabs/benno -> openai/alloy). Three Claude sessions were live in this repo, each with its own in-memory SessionConfig, all writing one shared per-repo vox.md, last writer wins. I called it 'per-repo config working as designed'. It is what unkeyed client state looks like from outside.

SO THE REAL WORK IS BIGGER THAN THIS BEAD. Move session state into voxd keyed by session; leave the MCP client holding only its own identity and the context it alone can originate (its repo, its session id), pushed to the engine. Then: staleness stops mattering much because the client holds nothing, sessions stop clobbering each other, and process management -- proxy or not -- becomes a free choice rather than a prerequisite.

DES-028's actual decision still stands: the daemon must not resolve CWDs from PIDs or guess which project a client is in. Keyed state does not reintroduce that -- the client PUSHES its identity, which is what invariant 4 prescribes.

This bead stays as the small, immediate piece: the WORKFLOW.md/CLAUDE.md doc gap and a visible version-drift check. The architectural work needs its own bead and a design pass.

title: Music widget intermittently replaces the 3-album catalog with a phantom 1-album 'Mix' row
description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-08-30 14:31) — this is a lux Hub defect, not vox.

The Hub never reaps a client connection whose process has died, and the orphaned
connection keeps ownership of its scenes and frames, shadowing the live client
that reconnects under the same identity.

  e888eb168472   voxd   connected=25.79h   scenes=['vox.music']   <- DEAD process
  222b70a5765a   voxd   connected= 0.18h   scenes=[]              <- live daemon, pid 189262

Exactly one voxd process and one socket to the hub exist (pid 189262, started
11 minutes earlier). The 25.79h connection belongs to a daemon that died the
previous day; voxd has been restarted TWICE since (13:51 and 14:26) and that
connection is still registered, still counting up, and still owning vox.music
and its frame. Its 30s lease is not evicting it.

This explains every symptom:

- The two album states. The window shows the DEAD daemon's last render -- 'Mix',
  techno, 0 tracks, a program that ran the previous day. The live daemon renders
  the catalog correctly but owns no scene, so its content only surfaces
  transiently before the zombie's frame is back on top.
- Nothing named 'Mix' exists on disk because it never was an album -- it is a
  stale in-memory render frozen in the Hub.
- No daemon push occurs during the flip because the daemon is not involved.
- 'luxd holds no vox.music frame to raise' on every install: the live connection
  genuinely has no frame, the zombie owns it. THIS IS ALSO THE CAUSE OF vox-640w.

Proved by instrumenting MusicPlayer._render in the installed package and
restarting the daemon. Over 3 minutes the live daemon logged three renders and
every one carried all 3 albums with correct counts, never 'Mix':

  PROBE render: 3 album(s) [('Molten Siege',0),('vox-h777 verification',0),('Realms Beyond the Map',0)]  caller=install
  PROBE render: 3 album(s) [('Molten Siege',8),('vox-h777 verification',12),('Realms Beyond the Map',12)] caller=_repaint_from_cache
  PROBE render: 3 album(s) [('Molten Siege',8),('vox-h777 verification',12),('Realms Beyond the Map',12)] caller=_refresh_track_counts

(Probe has been removed and the installed package restored; log level back to info.)

Ruled out along the way: a second voxd process; any remote host reaching the hub
(every socket on 8430 maps to a local pid, and the ssh forwards do not touch it);
a second scene on the Hub; a stale catalog (FilesystemProgramStore.scan yields
the 3 real albums); display-side errors (none buffered).

ACTIONS
1. lux: reap connections whose transport is gone; do not let an orphaned
   connection retain scene/frame ownership. Belongs in the lux repo.
2. vox-640w is very likely a duplicate symptom of this, not a vox bug -- verify
   against a hub with no zombie before doing any vox-side work on it.
3. Workaround until fixed: restart luxd to clear orphaned connections.

DEBUGGABILITY GAP: lux scopes scene inspection to the owning connection
(DES-086), so neither scene.inspect nor 'lux scene inspect --as' can read
another client's tree. Diagnosing this required patching the installed package.
A read-only inspection path would have made it a two-minute job.

=====================================================================
2026-08-30 15:00 -- EARLIER ROOT-CAUSE CLAIM RETRACTED. NOT YET FOUND.
=====================================================================

The 'orphaned voxd connection' theory above is DISPROVEN. The operator
restarted both luxd hub and luxd display; neither retains state across a
restart, and the flip still occurred afterwards (last seen 14:48:54).

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED (instrumented, not inferred)

MusicPlayer._render was patched in the installed package to log its album rows.
Across every render observed -- install, notify_changed, _repaint_from_cache,
_refresh_track_counts, row clicks, playback start, album switch -- the local
daemon rendered exactly the 3 real albums and NEVER 'Mix':
    [['Molten Siege', ..., 8], ['Vox H777 Verification', ..., 12],
     ['Realms Beyond The Map', ..., 12]]

The display DID hold a 'Mix' row. Proof: at 14:48:54 a click on it reached the
daemon as
    lux_subscription: anchor 'Mix' on music.play names no catalogued album; surfacing
and the resulting screenshot showed the notice 'couldn't play Mix -- no longer
in the crate' above a one-row table 'Mix | techno | 0'.

THE NARROW UNEXPLAINED FACT
Between 14:40:29 and 14:48:54 the vox daemon logged NO push of any kind, and
the Hub's scene set did not change (polled every 2s), yet the display's content
went from 3 albums to the 1-row 'Mix' table. Something changed displayed
content in a window where the only known producer sent nothing.

ALSO OBSERVED, POSSIBLY RELEVANT
- When the daemon DID re-render at 14:48:54 while the display showed 'Mix', it
  patched only 1 element (the notice) and left the table alone, because its
  LiveScene _previous said the table was already the 3-album one. So once the
  two diverge, diff-based pushes cannot correct it -- the divergence is sticky.
  A full install (menu click / reopen) does correct it.
- Every push is followed by 'vox.music scene unchanged; nothing pushed' from a
  second publisher pass.
- 'lux frame close <id>' returns success for a frame the caller does not own.
- vox logged 'luxd holds no vox.music frame to raise' at 14:15:32 while the
  display log recorded 'raise frame=...vox.music applied' at the same second.

RULED OUT
Second voxd process; any remote client on 8430 (every socket mapped to a local
pid); a second vox.music scene or frame on the Hub; a second vox.music frame id
in the display log (only e888eb168472139f has ever appeared); display-side
persisted state (none on disk); stale catalog (FilesystemProgramStore.scan
gives the 3 real albums); 'Mix'/'techno' anywhere on disk (absent).

CURRENT STATE
Stable since 14:49:32 (a menu-click install). It was also stable for ~8 minutes
after the 14:40:29 install before returning, so 'stable' is not yet 'fixed'.

LEFT IN PLACE FOR THE NEXT OCCURRENCE
- Probe in the INSTALLED package only:
  ~/.local/share/uv/tools/punt-vox/.../voxd/music_player/player.py logs
  'PROBE render albums=N rows=[...]'. Backup: /tmp/player.py.orig2. Any
  'make install' overwrites it. Daemon log level is debug.
- Watcher: .tmp/watch.sh -> .tmp/flip.log, recording Hub scene changes plus new
  display and vox log lines every 2s.
close_reason: Duplicate of vox-h7k8, which has the mechanism and the fix.

title: Session state lives in the MCP client, not the engine — violates architecture.md invariant 4
description:
Raised by Jim 2026-08-15: he does not want vox's code and state tied to the
Claude process lifecycle. The org standard already agrees, and vox is the outlier.

THE VIOLATION. punt-kit/standards/architecture.md, invariant 4 of the projection
model:

  "Client-specific state lives in the engine, keyed by client. Working directory,
   active repo, which features are on or off, session context -- the engine holds
   these authoritatively. A client carries only its own identity and the context
   it alone can originate... quarry keys each client's selected database
   server-side: the `quarry serve` daemon holds it, not the client."

vox does the opposite. DES-028 states it plainly: "MCP server: Lightweight stdio
process per Claude Code session. Session state in memory." `SessionConfig`
(server.py:112) holds ten fields -- session_id, notify, speak, voice, provider,
model, vibe_mode, vibe, vibe_tags, speak_explicit -- inside a stdio subprocess
that Claude Code spawns, owns, and kills.

quarry is the cited reference doing this correctly. vox is the exception.

WHAT IT HAS ALREADY COST -- two separate incidents on one day, both initially
misdiagnosed by me as something else:

  1. CONFIG CLOBBERING. Jim's provider/voice changed under him mid-session
     (elevenlabs/benno -> openai/alloy, speak n -> y). Three Claude sessions were
     live in this repo, each holding its own in-memory SessionConfig, all writing
     one shared per-repo vox.md. Last writer wins. I called it "per-repo config
     working as designed" -- it is unkeyed client state seen from outside.
  2. INVISIBLE VERSION SKEW (vox-r1fv). A session's MCP server keeps serving the
     code it was spawned with. `mic:status` lacked a block that `vox doctor`
     showed, from the same install, because one is a fresh process and the other
     is not. If the client held no state and no logic, this would be a restart,
     not a debugging session.

THE CHANGE. Move session state into voxd, keyed by session. The MCP client keeps
only what it alone can originate -- its session id and its repo -- and pushes
that to the engine, exactly as invariant 4 prescribes. Then the MCP process
becomes disposable: sessions stop clobbering each other, staleness stops
mattering much, and process management (mcp-proxy or anything else) becomes a
free choice rather than a prerequisite.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REOPEN. DES-028 replaced the v2 mcp-proxy design because that
daemon tried to KNOW which project a client belonged to -- resolving CWDs from
PIDs via lsof, ContextVars, 8 rounds of path bugs. That decision stands and this
does not reverse it. The difference is direction: v2 had the daemon GUESS the
client's context; invariant 4 has the client PUSH it. Any design here must
preserve that and must not reintroduce CWD/PID resolution in the daemon.

NEEDS A DESIGN PASS BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. Open questions worth settling first:
what is the session key and who mints it; what happens to vox.md and
vox.local.md when the engine is authoritative (per-repo durable prefs vs
per-session ephemeral state is exactly the confusion that produced incident 1);
whether hooks and the CLI become keyed clients too; and what a client sees when
it reconnects to a daemon that has been restarted. This is a stateful subsystem
with modes and invariants, so it likely qualifies for the z-spec gate in
CLAUDE.md.
notes:
CARRIES AN OWED DESIGN DECISION from vox-otj9, 2026-08-15.

Jim ratified a design for the provider/model pair that has NOT been built. It
belongs here rather than in otj9, because this bead restructures the same area
and building it twice is waste.

THE RATIFIED DESIGN. provider and model become ONE value object. Changing the
provider RETURNS a new value whose model is the new provider's default, so a
stale pair cannot be constructed:

    engine.with_provider("polly")   # model is polly's default, never eleven_v3
    engine.with_model("tts-1")      # validated against THIS provider; F7 lives here, once

Jim chose this over two alternatives (a NullModel-only change, and per-provider
model resolution) after rejecting my first answer as bad design. His reasoning:
the cascade rule "new provider resets the model" is ALREADY implemented three
separate times -- server_switches._commit_provider, panel/service._commit_provider,
and mic:provider -- precisely because two independent values that must agree keep
drifting. A fourth correction site does not remove the possibility; making the
bad state unconstructable does. The value object deletes the three duplicates.

Pair it with a Null Object for the modelless case: ProviderModels already exists
in models.py and polly/say/espeak are already full=(). Make it ANSWER the
question (default() returns a Model; the empty set returns NullModel, PY-DP-9)
instead of making callers test for emptiness. `model: str | None` then leaves the
system, and modelless becomes a polymorphic answer rather than a special case.

WHY IT LANDED HERE. vox-otj9 shipped a narrower fix -- SessionSpec consults
state's model only when the resolved provider matches state's provider. It is
tested (20-case matrix over every ordered provider pair) and it closes the live
P1, but it corrects the drift rather than preventing it. It went in because two
messages carrying the ratified design never reached the worker (biff was timing
out) and the P1 was live in production. Recording that plainly: this was a
messaging failure of mine, not a design reversal, and Jim's ratification stands.

CONSTRAINT FOR WHOEVER DESIGNS THIS. The value object and the session-state
relocation interact: if state moves into voxd keyed by session, the pair should
be authoritative THERE, and the client should not be able to hold a half-updated
copy. Design them together.

title: A .tex file with no Z paragraphs type-checks clean
description:
fuzz -t on a .tex containing no Z paragraphs exits 0 with empty output. run_fuzz returns FuzzResult(ok=True, errors=[], raw_output='') and the Makefile prints the tick, so 'there was nothing to check' is reported to the user as 'it type-checked'.

MEASURED, during the silent-failure review of the model-check gate work. fuzz's exit code is otherwise SOUND and does not need changing: rc 1 on a type error, rc 1 on an undeclared identifier, rc 1 on a syntax error, rc 2 on a missing file. Unlike probcli, fuzz does not exit 0 after reporting a fault. Nobody should re-investigate that half.

The gap is the other kind: a caller cannot distinguish 'found nothing wrong' from 'did not look'. A missing \usepackage{fuzz} IS caught. These are not: a mis-scoped \begin{document}, a commented-out block, a refactor that empties a file, or a spec whose environments stop being recognised for any other reason. In each case make type-z-<stem> prints the tick and the lux fuzz tab shows a clean result.

REPAIR. parser.py already builds a SpecModel carrying the schema list. Nothing compares it to the fuzz result. The check is to require that a spec fuzz reports clean actually contained something to check, and to report 'no Z paragraphs found' otherwise — a distinct verdict, not a pass and not a type error.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE GATE WORK. It is the same defect class in a different gate, and by the org rule it belonged to that change once seen. It was left out on sizing: it needs a comparison between two subsystems that do not currently talk, where every other defect in that change was contained to how one tool's output was read. It was assigned for sizing and the session ended before it was scoped.

RELATED. The same review found the probcli half of this class — four checks whose verdict came from an exit status probcli does not set — which is fixed. This is the fuzz half and it is the last known instance.

Found by the silent-failure review, 2026-08-08. Filed by claude.

title: claude-code.tex: maxContext=200 is a production value in an animation-bound field
description:
claude-code.tex sets maxContext = 200. All four of its derivatives set 3.

    claude-code.tex   maxTools 20  maxSubagents 10  maxContext 200
    the other four    maxTools  5  maxSubagents  2  maxContext   3

The axdef's own comment reads 'Bounds for ProB animation.' 200 is not an animation bound; it is a plausible production value that wandered into a field reserved for animation bounds, which is exactly what the comment beside it warns against.

EFFECT. It is the direct cause of the model_check_incomplete warning on the corpus's flagship spec. CompactContext(newLen?) is guarded by newLen? < # context and newLen? <= maxContext, so a state with a full context has up to 200 enabled instances of that one operation, against a gate ceiling of exactly MAX_OPERATIONS=200. The spec's bound and the gate's ceiling are the same number by coincidence. With DEFAULT_SETSIZE 1 the CONTEXTCHUNK carrier has one element, so a sequence of length <= 200 over it is 201 distinct values, which is where the 329k states come from.

MEASURED by jms, scratch copy, maxContext the only change:

    maxContext = 200:  329362 states,  1181562 transitions,  warning
    maxContext =   3:    2007 states,     6677 transitions,  ALL states visited
                         UNCOVERED_OPERATIONS (0), COVERED_OPERATIONS (21)
                         deadlocked:0, invariant_violated:0

164x fewer states, 177x fewer transitions, all 21 operations still covered, warning gone with margin. Nothing is lost: the same operations fire, and the invariants then hold over the WHOLE reachable space rather than over a certifiably-incomplete one. It also takes roughly three minutes off every make check in this repo, since claude-code dominates the spec tier.

WHY IT IS A SPEC FIX AND NOT A MAKEFILE CHANGE. Raising MAX_OPERATIONS would preserve a 329362-state model of a 2007-state machine and buy nothing but a longer wait. The structure of the document is fine — the four derivatives carry every operation the parent does, plus their own layer, at 10k-24k states. One constant is wrong.

THE JUDGEMENT THIS NEEDS, and it is why this is a bead rather than a one-line commit. Nobody has checked whether the document's prose depends on maxContext being 200, and 3 is a small number for a context window in a file people read to understand Claude Code. If the 200 is there to be READ rather than to be animated, the honest repair is TWO constants — the animation bound and the documented capacity — not one retuned. Decide which the file is for before changing it.

RELATED CONTEXT. The warning was found while verifying m-2026-08-09-011 and is genuinely harmless on this run: jms re-ran at MAX_OPERATIONS 400 and got identical state and transition counts with 'ALL states visited', so the 200 run was complete and merely could not certify itself. Coverage results are monotone under exploration and survive truncation; no-counterexample, deadlocked:0 and invariant_violated:0 are universal claims and do not. Diagnosis by jms (Spivey); filed by claude.

title: Add non-blocking CI verification for the installer and for plugin-install cleanliness (macOS + Linux)
description:
Follow-on to z-spec-68e (probcli setup fix, PR #150). While fixing that bug we
established strong evidence the Linux install path works (a real probcli
1.15.1 binary was downloaded and run, and CI's own specs job independently
installs and runs the same binary on every push) but only weak, metadata-level
evidence for macOS (URL/content-type/size checks and a zip-listing read via
HTTP Range requests — nothing was ever actually downloaded, unzipped, or run
on a Mac), and zero automated coverage of setup.md's *literal* documented
commands on either platform (this dev sandbox blocks outbound curl for every
agent, confirmed independently twice during that PR).

Ruled with the operator (2026-08-28): release the probcli fix first, do this
work as a separate follow-on — not blocking that release.

Two genuinely separate concerns, both new and unrelated to existing CI
(lint.yml, test.yml already prove the code is internally consistent, assuming
a probcli binary already exists by whatever fast means test.yml's own install
step uses — that step is infrastructure to unblock other tests, not itself
under test, and should not be conflated with this work):

1. **Installer verification job.** On a clean `ubuntu-latest` and a clean
   `macos-latest` runner, actually run the real install instructions from
   plugin/commands/setup.md (extracted into a shared script both the doc and
   this job invoke, e.g. scripts/install-probcli.sh / install-lean.sh, so the
   doc and the tested code cannot drift — the same failure class z-spec-68e
   just fixed) and assert the end state: binary present, executable, correct
   pinned version. Do the same for the elan/lean install path.

2. **Plugin-install cleanliness job.** On a clean checkout, actually run the
   real marketplace install mechanism (claude plugin install / the git-subdir
   sparse-checkout path this repo's CLAUDE.md documents) on both platforms and
   assert the sparse-checkout invariant currently only claimed in prose: only
   plugin/ lands on the user's disk, nothing from src/, tests/, tools/, docs/,
   examples/, research/, .punt-labs/, or .claude/ leaks. Currently zero
   automated coverage of this claim.

Both jobs will be slow (ProB's archive alone is 42-56MB; a first Lean build
pulls a ~2GB dependency cache) and must be non-blocking to normal PR
integration per the operator's explicit instruction — continue-on-error,
workflow_dispatch, or scheduled, not a required check on every push. Try it
and measure actual runtime rather than guessing at the right triggering
strategy up front.

This needs a design pass before implementation (new CI architecture,
extraction of shared install scripts, cross-platform runner behavior) - not a
quick fix. Worker/evaluator pairing per this repo's ownership table: CLI/CI
work maps to mdm (worker) / adb (evaluator) for the workflow/packaging pieces;
the extracted install scripts themselves are rmh (worker) / gvr (evaluator)
per the Python ownership row, though these are shell scripts, not Python -
use judgment on the split when scoping the design mission.

title: fuzz install: eliminate sudo requirement via user-prefixed build
description:
Investigation 2026-08-30: pulled Spivoxity/fuzz's actual Makefile.in from GitHub. Its install target uses standard autoconf prefix/bindir/datadir variables that default to root-owned /usr/local when ./configure is run with no --prefix -- that default, not anything inherent to fuzz, is why our setup.md/install.sh instructions say sudo make install.

Fix: ./configure --prefix=$HOME/.local installs the fuzz binary and fuzz.sty entirely into user-writable paths. Point the texmf output at kpsewhich -var-value TEXMFHOME (the personal tree every TeX Live install already searches, no texhash/sudo needed) or copy tex/fuzz.sty + tex/*.mf there post-build and run mktexlsr on that one directory (no sudo).

This removes sudo from the entire fuzz setup path. Once nothing needs root, the earlier 'must stay a human-typed procedure, outside the agent's allowed-tools' framing in setup.md dissolves -- the whole build (git clone, make, copy, mktexlsr) can become agent-runnable and, ideally, auto-provisioned by install.sh the same way probcli already is (see resolve_probcli-equivalent for fuzz).

Scope: rewrite install.sh's fuzz section (currently deliberately non-installing, per its own comments) and plugin/commands/setup.md's 'Install fuzz' section (currently framed as human-only). Update doctor.py/setup.md's allowed-tools if the build becomes agent-runnable. Companion beads: z-spec-gwv (add failure guards to the now-scriptable install), z-spec-qnc (manual-tests.md row for /z-spec:setup, written against the new sudo-free flow).

title: Lux: applet name stamps its own pid, not the session pid — z-spec never merges into the session's Clients submenu
description: Reported by lux agent (claude:tty11) via biff 2026-08-31. ZSpecLuxIdentity (src/punt_zspec/lux/identity.py:46) passes session_pid=os.getpid() — the MCP server's OWN pid — into applet_name_format.format_name. Lux groups Clients-menu entries by the session pid parsed from the applet name (session_pid_from_name -> MenuGroupKey), so z-spec's applet never shares a group with the same session's vox-panel (which stamps the real session pid via --session-pid). description: The Tutorial menu callback (0.18.0, feat/lux-normal-path-client) loads the shipped tutorials/ manifest via __file__, which resolves in-repo but is not wheel-safe — an installed punt-z-spec would not find the manifest through __file__ if package data is not laid out to match. title: source? and reason? are declared and discarded in all five session specs
description:
In examples/claude-code.tex and its four derivatives, the inputs source? : SessionStartSource and reason? : SessionEndReason are declared and typed, and then never used. jra verified by scan: each occurs only on its declaration line.

    claude-code.tex   :285  :796
    claude-code-biff  :294  :1051
    claude-code-lux   :284  :867
    claude-code-quarry :286 :321  :899
    claude-code-vox   :278  :909

No predicate constrains either input. No state variable records either. So SessionStartSource (4 values) and SessionEndReason (5 values) have no observable consequence anywhere in the corpus — the specs declare that a session can start four ways and end five ways, and then model all four starts identically and all five ends identically.

This is the same defect jms repaired in the quarry spec, moved from state into inputs. There, three config flags were declared as state and then pinned constant, so the behaviour they were supposed to distinguish was unreachable. Here the distinction is declared as an input and then dropped.

The coverage census cannot detect it. EndSession fired 5025 times in the base spec run, so every operation is covered and the gate is green while five distinguishable reasons collapse into one. That bounds what the census proves: every operation fires, not every declared distinction is observable.

The sharpest case is ssClear and seClear. They name the two halves of one real transition — /clear ends a session and immediately starts another. The model exhibits neither. And because spEnded is terminal, ssClear can only ever label the machine's first session, which is the one case where nothing was cleared.

This blocks a better fix elsewhere. jra built ClearSession (spEnded to spInactive) as a domain-grounded alternative to the SessionOver halt schema and measured it clean at 10161 states / 58007 transitions / 28 operations covered on the lux spec. He rejected it because it is only correct for seClear, and the model cannot restrict it to that reason while reason? is discarded. As written it would assert that a session ended by logout may be followed by another in the same machine, which is false. With the reason recorded, /clear becomes a real transition and the declared halt narrows to logout and exit.

Repair: record the reason in state at EndSession, and the source at StartSession, then let ClearSession be guarded on seClear. Check afterwards that the census still reaches every operation and that no new deadlock appears.

Found by jra (Abrial) while evaluating m-2026-08-09-011. Filed by claude.

title: cbc_assertions may be structurally incapable of failing on a Z specification
description:
run_full_suite runs six checks. One of them, cbc_assertions, may never be able to fail on any Z input, which would make it a sixth check that cannot fail inside a change whose entire subject is checks that cannot fail.

MEASUREMENT, by rmh, one experiment only. A fuzz-clean specification carrying a deliberately false theorem — asserting maxCount = 99 where the axdef fixes maxCount == 2 — was run through probcli -cbc_assertions. probcli reported 'No counter-example to ASSERTION exists'. The false theorem was not detected.

INFERENCE, unconfirmed: ProB's Z front end does not translate fuzz 'theorem' paragraphs into checkable assertions. If that holds, no Z specification can produce a cbc_assertions failure, because the theorem paragraph is the only mechanism Z has for declaring one.

WHY THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT A FIX. One measurement, on one construction of a false theorem, against one probcli version (1.15.1). The inference could be wrong in several ways: the theorem might need a different form, ProB might require a directive to enable assertion checking, or the Z front end might handle some assertion syntaxes and not others. Encoding 'this check cannot fail' in code on that evidence would be the same error as the defects being repaired — a conclusion asserted rather than measured. rmh declined to do it and was right to.

FOR jra. The question is about ProB's Z front end, not about the Python. Confirm or refute: can any Z specification produce a counter-example from -cbc_assertions? If yes, produce the specification and the transcript, and a failing fixture follows from it. If no, the honest outcomes are either to remove cbc_assertions from run_full_suite, or to keep it and state in the report that it is inert for Z input — but not to leave it presented beside five checks that can fail, indistinguishable from them.

CONSEQUENCE ALREADY IN THE TREE. tests/fixtures/probcli/ now carries failing transcripts for init, animate and cbc_deadlock, and cannot carry one for cbc_assertions. The README records the absence and this reason rather than leaving it silent. That note should be updated or removed once this bead resolves.

RELATED. The rule in TESTING.md — a gate must be shown failing before it is trusted — is what surfaced this: four of six checks had no failing fixture, three were then produced, and the fourth could not be.

Found by rmh (Hettinger) while repairing the gate. Filed by claude for jra (Abrial).

title: z-spec model-check: pass extra args to probcli, drop named knobs
description:
One CLI:

    z-spec model-check <spec> [-- <extra probcli args>]

Wrapper hardcodes -model_check, -coverage, DEFAULT_SETSIZE=1, MAX_OPERATIONS=1000, TIME_OUT=1800000, MAX_INITIALISATIONS=20. Anything after -- is appended and wins.

Delete --setsize, --max-ops, --timeout. Nobody who needs them will suffer; they pass -p or -card.

MCP tool grows one field: extra_args: list[str] = [].

That's it. No allowlist, no collision check, no dataclass gymnastics.

Supersedes z-spec-grx (closed) and probably z-spec-51t (re-measure after this lands).

Filed by claude — simpler rewrite of z-spec-o6i (closed).

title: Every agent-team teammate spawns a z-spec MCP server + lux applet — Clients menu fills with duplicate repo entries
description: Observed 2026-08-30 in vox: with tmux teammate mode, each spawned teammate is a full Claude process that boots the entire plugin stack, so every teammate adds a z-spec mcp process and a lux applet connection registering Z-Spec Browser/Tutorial menu entries. The lux Clients menu showed vox, vox (2) through vox (8) — six z-spec applet connections from one repo, most belonging to short-lived worker teammates; connections persist as long as the teammate process idles. Cost: process-per-teammate overhead and an unusable Clients menu. Possible directions: skip applet/menu registration in subagent sessions (detect via CLAUDE_* env or session type), or dedupe menu registration per repo, or make registrations expire with a short idle TTL. Cross-repo observation from vox (leader session vox-eb); lux may need a companion change for menu dedup/expiry.

title: states_analysed and transitions_fired conflate 'probcli said zero' with 'probcli said nothing'
description:
ProbOutput.states_analysed and transitions_fired return 0 when the regex finds no match, so a caller cannot tell a run probcli reported zero states for from a run that printed no such line. Every -animate run is the second case: probcli does not print a state count for an animation, so every animate applet renders 'States: 0 | Transitions: 0 | Result: PASS'.

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN THE RENDERER. model-check-counter-example.out genuinely reports 'States analysed: 0' — zero is a real measured value there. So no rendering rule can separate the two cases; the distinction has to exist in the data.

REPAIR. int | None on ProbOutput.states_analysed and transitions_fired and on the two ProbReport fields, with the PY-TS-14 justification that absence is the documented contract: probcli either printed the line or it did not, and that is an answer rather than a parser failing to produce a value. This is the sanctioned use of Optional, not the pattern PY-TS-14 exists to discourage.

BLAST RADIUS, counted: six source and test files. prob_output.py (two properties), types/prob.py (two fields plus to_dict), report.py (two .get defaults), applet.py (the two cards), and the assertions in tests/test_prob_output.py, tests/test_prob.py, tests/test_report.py, tests/types/test_prob.py and tests/test_applet.py that currently expect 0.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DONE. It misreports on screen; it cannot mis-verdict. Unlike the sibling defects repaired in the same change — a coverage ratio computed from a census that does not exist, and four checks whose verdict came from an exit status probcli does not set — this one cannot pass a broken specification. It was separated on that basis and because it was the only remaining item that could not be typed by hand in the session available.

The coverage half of the same defect IS fixed: the metrics card now says 'Coverage: not measured' rather than '0/0 ops', and the absent per-operation table is labelled.

Found by the silent-failure review of the model-check gate work. Diagnosis and sizing by rmh (Hettinger).

title: SDK test tier: drive a real model through the command prompts
description:
PL-TT-1 defines a tier 4 — end-to-end with a live model, opt-in, costs money. z-spec has no harness for it and no pytest markers configured.

tests/commands/test_prompt_contracts.py covers what can be asserted about a prompt without running one: internal consistency, so a document that both specifies a protocol and embeds a reference implementation cannot contradict itself. That is deterministic and free, and it caught the oracle verdict bug.

What it cannot cover is the interesting half. Given a spec, does /z-spec:oracle actually make the model emit Lean that compiles, and does that binary actually speak the protocol the prompt describes? A prompt can be perfectly self-consistent and still fail to elicit the behaviour. Nothing in the current pyramid touches that gap, for any of the 21 commands.

Sketch:

- A fixture spec under examples/ small enough to run cheaply, and currently absent — nothing exercises /z-spec:oracle even by hand, so the acceptance flight has no row for it.
- Drive the command via the Agent SDK against that fixture.
- Assert the emitted Lean compiles under lake, that the binary emits NDJSON with the verdict envelope, and that a precondition violation reports ok:false with a reason.
- Gate behind an sdk pytest marker, deselected by default, alongside the existing e2e marker. Not in make check; costs real money per run.

Worth doing for /z-spec:oracle first, since it has a machine-checkable output contract. Most other commands emit prose or LaTeX, where the assertion is far weaker — decide per command rather than assuming the tier generalises.

Related: the deterministic tier is z-spec-dbk's PR.
notes: 2026-08-30 (claude): re-verified — the bead's 'fixture spec absent' claim is now false (examples/oracle-protocol.tex + .fuzz + .report.json all exist). The actual harness (SDK-driven test asserting Lean compiles + NDJSON envelope) still doesn't exist. Downgraded from P2: opt-in, costs real money per run, blocks nothing current.

title: EPIC: correctness sweep — false passes, ProB 1.16 unpin, inert gate, spec-corpus bugs, probcli passthrough
description: Sprint 1 PR-B as an epic. Six children: z-spec-2mm (P1 false pass on Z-paragraph-free .tex), z-spec-v0m (coverage parser vs ProB >=1.16 — the reason probcli is pinned to 1.15.1), z-spec-edh (cbc_assertions may be structurally unable to fail on Z input — jra ruling needed), z-spec-51t (claude-code.tex maxContext=200 state explosion — direct cause of the 5-7min specs CI legs; re-measure after hhm), z-spec-cbg (source?/reason? declared and discarded in all five session specs), z-spec-hhm (probcli extra-args passthrough, drop named knobs; do FIRST, then re-measure 51t). Rollback-coherent as one PR per sprint-plan; split only if it grows unwieldy.

title: Explore: push z-spec functionality into deterministic code paths (L1 tools for L4 agents)
description:
Inspired by https://www.pkit-labs.com/blog/building-l1-tools-for-l4-agents

## Current State
z-spec is a pure plugin — all prompt-driven skills, no runtime code. The LLM generates LaTeX Z specs from scratch every time (L4). The only L1 tools are external binaries (fuzz, probcli). The verification gap exists in every line of LaTeX the LLM writes.

## The Opportunity
Apply the Lux boundary pattern: the LLM describes WHAT (state variables, invariants, operations as structured data), deterministic code produces HOW (syntactically correct LaTeX, valid hook wiring, passing type-checks).

## Candidate L1 Tools

### Spec Generation (reduce LLM to data mapping)
- **Template engine**: Takes structured input (state vars, free types, operations, invariants) as JSON/YAML and produces syntactically correct fuzz-compatible LaTeX. The LLM fills in a data structure; the tool writes correct syntax. Eliminates classes of bugs: \\t1 vs \\quad~, missing frame conditions, inconsistent primed variables.
- **Hook-to-Z translator**: Reads hooks.json + hooks.py and auto-generates the Hook Event Map section and skeleton operation schemas. The LLM refines invariants and preconditions; the tool handles boilerplate.

### Validation (catch errors before model-checking)
- **Convention checker**: Lint Z specs for project conventions — bounded sets, ZBOOL usage, no \\t1, frame conditions present, all primed variables assigned. Faster than probcli, catches common mistakes immediately.
- **Coverage auditor**: Compare hooks.json registrations against Z spec operations. Flag dead handlers (handler exists, no registration) and orphan operations (operation exists, no handler). This is the audit that found quarry's wiring gap — automate it.

### Code Generation (from spec to implementation)
- **Hook scaffold generator**: Given a Z spec with PreToolUse/Stop/PostToolUse operations, generate the hooks.json entries, shell dispatcher scripts, and Python handler skeletons. The LLM fills in business logic; the tool handles wiring.
- **Test generator**: From Z spec operation preconditions, generate pytest test cases that verify the handler respects the preconditions. Each \\where clause becomes a test assertion.

## The Ratio Target
Like Lux (40 lines agentic / 2000 lines deterministic), aim for:
- LLM writes: state variable names, invariant predicates, operation semantics (the WHAT)
- Tool writes: LaTeX syntax, frame conditions, hooks.json, shell scripts, Python boilerplate (the HOW)

## Design Questions
1. Should the structured input be JSON, YAML, or a DSL?
2. Should the template engine be a Python CLI (following cli.md) or a prompt-driven skill that calls MCP tools?
3. Which candidate tool has the highest ROI? (Convention checker is probably lowest effort, highest immediate value)
4. Does this change z-spec from a pure plugin to a CLI+plugin hybrid?

## References
- Blog post: building-l1-tools-for-l4-agents.md
- Lux architecture: 22 built-in elements, LLM writes data mapping only
- Current z-spec audit findings: \\t1 bug, ghost states, context overflow — all preventable by L1 tooling
- cli.md projection strategy: CLI is source of truth, MCP/plugin projects it

title: src/punt_zspec/coverage.py cannot parse ProB >=1.16.0's coverage census output — every spec silently fails coverage check on current ProB
description:
coverage.py's _CENSUS_RE (r"\[STATES \(\d+\),[^\]]*\]") parses ProB's -coverage
output as a single bracketed line. ProB 1.16.0 changed that output to a
multi-line table:

    Coverage Information:
    CATEGORY HITS
    STATES 11
    ...
    COVERED_OPERATIONS 7
    AddAssignment 24

Bisected against real probcli binaries (1.15.1-final vs 1.16.0-final): the
bracketed form disappears exactly at 1.16.0. On 1.16.x the model-check itself
still runs and every operation still fires, but z-spec reports
"coverage: failed -- probcli printed no coverage census" / "0 operations" on
every spec, even though ProB genuinely covered them.

Discovered while fixing z-spec-68e (the probcli setup installer downloaded a
dead URL). The installer fix (PR pending) works around this by pinning
probcli to 1.15.1 instead of the current 1.16.1, with an in-doc note
explaining why and pointing back at this bead. That pin note should be
deleted once this parser reads the new table format, so z-spec can move to
current ProB releases again.

Fix: extend/replace _CENSUS_RE (or the coverage parsing path around it) to
also recognize the tabular CATEGORY/HITS format, ideally by parsing on
semantic content (STATES/COVERED_OPERATIONS rows) rather than a line-shape
regex, so a future ProB output reformat doesn't reopen this. Worker: rmh
per this repo's Python ownership table.
